Ty Pennington renovating a home in 2007. (GC Images)
When tackling home projects and renovation with his wife, Kellee Merrell, Pennington said compromise can prevent them from budding heads.
TIM MCGRAW WARNS OF ‘MOST DANGEROUS’ TIMES IN MARRIAGE AFTER 30 YEARS WITH FAITH HILL

"Sometimes you have to divide and conquer," Pennington said. "If somebody is passionate about a certain project that they know exactly what they think they want it to look like, sometimes you have to just use a different room in a different project. We don't always agree on everything. I don't think that happens in any aspect of life. What I try and do is lend my perspective and also throw out a couple of crazy ideas that hopefully sometimes lead to something sort of midway between."
"When you're dealing with a spouse and their plans, you sort of have to just be like, well, you just have to trust," he added. "And I think that's the key."
Ty Pennington and Kellee Merrell tied the knot in November 2021. (Ty Pennington Instagram)
These days, Pennington is splitting his time between his home in Georgia with Merrell and his mother’s home in Florida, where he has stepped into a caretaker role.
Nearly 20 years ago, his mother was officially diagnosed with bronchiectasis, or BE—a chronic, progressive lung condition that causes permanent widening and scarring of the airways.

Pennington, who has partnered with biopharmaceutical company Insmed as a spokesperson to raise awareness and educate others about BE, said his mother's diagnosis—combined with his own past health scare involving a life-threatening throat abscess—fundamentally shifted his perspective on life.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Pennington has taken the role of caretaker for his mother, who was diagnosed with BE 20 years ago. (Ty Pennington Instagram)

"[The diagnosis] certainly is an eye-opener, and you realize, 'My God, you really don't know what life's going to throw you around the next corner,'" Pennington said. "Just having the thing that happened to me on my throat and finding out that people can die of that just makes you realize everything is fleeting. Honestly, what it reassures you is that you really have to live life to the fullest, and you have to make every moment you can share with your loved ones the best."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"You have to get more of that laughter and more of that fun in your lives," he continued. "I think having clarity and understanding what you're dealing with is so important so that you can focus on those better, fun times. I have a little bit of regret because we didn't realize what was going on for so long with my mom. We only have so much time in life. Let's make the best of it."
Pennington says his mother's diagnosis changed the way he thinks about his own health. (Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images for SCAD)
Watching his mother navigate a chronic respiratory condition has also shifted his own mindset when it comes to staying physically active.

"I think it's really important to make sure you take time to focus on your body and make sure you're constantly moving," he said. "The one thing I've noticed with my mom is because you're battling and struggling with some health issues, you don't keep your body as strong as it should be because you get winded."

"What I've learned from that is if you have the capability of keeping your body in shape—constantly moving, constantly exercising—it is going to make sure you can add a few extra years to your life," Pennington added. "That's what I'm trying to do, as well as trying to motivate my mom to keep moving as well. Luckily, I stay very active and I've always been really active. You have to worry a little bit more about injuries because of that, so it's never too late to wear a helmet every day. I'm kidding, but you get the idea."

title: Tommy Lee Jones says ‘God loved me’ by putting him in Texas, opens up about life on his 6,000-acre ranch
summary: Tommy Lee Jones said he knew God loved him "because he put me on the ground in Texas," where he now lives and is raising 25 horses and has two polo fields.
story: Jones moved back to Texas in the early 2000s. (Rick Kern/Getty Images)
Tommy Lee Jones is discussing his decision to live on a ranch in his Texas hometown and one of his hobbies that has carried over since the '70s.

During a recent interview with The New York Times, the 80-year-old actor shared how he decided to move back to San Saba, Texas, in the early 2000s, saying, "I knew that God loved me because he put me on the ground in Texas."
"There came a time when I became aware that I could live anywhere I wanted to," Jones said. "So, in my wisdom, I went home."

The actor now lives on a 6,000-acre ranch in a two-story home originally built in 1856 and has turned it into the home he always wanted, noting he wanted to live somewhere that didn't have "any fences around the house."
Jones moved back to Texas in the early 2000s. (Rick Kern/Getty Images)
ANTONIO BANDERAS SAYS HE ALWAYS KNEW LOS ANGELES WASN'T WHERE HE BELONGED

When speaking to the outlet, the "No Country for Old Men" star shared that living on the ranch also allowed him to enjoy playing polo. The actor grew up riding horses and began playing polo in the 1970s.
Since moving onto his ranch, Jones has built two polo fields on the property, which now also holds 25 horses, and the actor and his wife, Dawn Laurel-Jones, host many polo events throughout the year.
Jones and Dawn Laurel-Jones have been married 25 years. (Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic)
Although Jones doesn't compete anymore, his wife continues to participate in competitions.
"She’s one of the better female polo players in the United States," Jones said of his wife.
Jones was an avid polo player and has two polo fields on his ranch. (Chris Weeks/Getty Images)
Jones began playing polo in the 1970s and grew up riding horses. (Chris Weeks/Liaison)

Jones started his acting career in the 1970s, making a name for himself as a cast member on the soap opera "One Life to Live," and appeared in many acclaimed television projects, winning an Emmy Award in 1983 for his work on "The Executioner's Song."

He cemented his status as a leading man and Hollywood heavyweight in the 1990s, earning his first of four Academy Award nominations in 1992 for his role in "JFK." He won the award for best supporting actor in 1994 for his work in "The Fugitive."
Jones won an Academy Award for his supporting role in "The Fugitive" in 1994. (Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

Despite his prolific acting career, Jones told Esquire in November he isn't concerned with the "legacy" he is leaving behind.
"I don’t have long-term thinking, and I don’t even think in a term like legacy," he said. "I think more like a dog. I’m absorbed with what’s in front of me. I might run off and chase a squirrel."
Jones is not concerned with his legacy. (Phillip Faraone/Getty Images)
He is starring in the FX show, "The Lowdown," alongside Ethan Hawke, Betty Gilpin and Jeanne Tripplehorn.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
The actor portrays Ethan Hawke's dad, Lee Raybon Sr., who goes by Frog and has recently returned to his son's life following a period of separation.
Jones is starring in the second season of "The Lowdown" with Ethan Hawke. (Rick Kern/Getty Images)

"We learn that this character is dying," he said. "That slowly begins to dawn on us, and we see that he’s trying to somehow reconcile life with his son and get to know his granddaughter. But that quest in this character is not advertised. It’s discovered as we watch things unfold in an often amusing way, and always original. That was appealing. I mean, I think that’s the way it works."

Earlier this year, the actor's daughter, Victoria Jones, was found dead in a San Francisco hotel room on Jan. 1. The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner confirmed to Fox News Digital in February that she died because of "toxic effects of cocaine," and that her death was ruled an "accident."
After news of Victoria's sudden death broke, Tommy Lee broke his silence in a statement shared with Fox News Digital.

Jones' daughter, Victoria, died in January. (Stephane Cardinale/Corbis)
In addition to Victoria, Jones is a father to his son Austin, whom he shares with his ex-wife, Kimberlea Cloughley.

title: Bo Derek stands by falling for married John Derek at 16 despite 30-year age gap: 'It all worked out'
summary: Bo Derek reflects on meeting married director John Derek at 16, while "Dynasty" star Linda Evans recalls the devastation of losing him on a Greek film set.
story: John and Bo Derek pose together in Qatar on March 23, 1996. (Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images)
Bo Derek believes "it all worked out" when it comes to her marriage to John Derek, the director who was 46 and married when she met him as a 16-year-old up-and-coming actress.
She spoke about their relationship — as did John's former wife, "Dynasty" star Linda Evans — in a new profile for The Hollywood Reporter.
John, best known for appearing alongside Charlton Heston in "The Ten Commandments," had shifted into filmmaking later in his career.
In the early 1970s, he'd set out to cast a movie he'd written, "Fantasies," about a relationship between a teenage girl and her adoptive brother.
CAMERON MATHISON SAYS HE HAS ‘TONS’ IN COMMON WITH NEW GIRLFRIEND TAELYR ROBINSON DESPITE 24-YEAR AGE GAP
Bo Derek met John Derek when she was 16 at an audition for a movie he was directing. (Getty Images)

Bo, who went by her birth name, Mary Cathleen Collins, at the time, auditioned and was given the part. The film was shot in Greece, but John asked Evans to give Bo acting lessons before they departed.
As Evans recalled, Bo was "beautifully independent," and she had "zero, zero, zero" suspicions that anything romantic might develop between the teen and her husband at the time.
"I was with him 25 years until he died. He was a very ridiculously honest, good man. And it all worked out, didn’t it?"
Bo told the outlet her relationship with John and the age gap they shared is "not the natural way of things.
"If it were my daughter, I would have kidnapped her and taken her away from him, of course," Bo said.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Bo admitted that if she had a daughter, she wouldn't approve of her getting involved with a man 30 years her elder. (Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images)
"At the same time, I was with him 25 years until he died. He was a very ridiculously honest, good man. And it all worked out, didn’t it?"
It was 1973 when Bo left with John for Europe to shoot the film. A few weeks later, Evans traveled to visit John on the set, which was when she'd learned that he'd fallen for Bo.
Linda Evans with John Derek in 1972, a year before their marriage ended when he started seeing Bo Derek. (Getty Images)
"To say I was devastated is an understatement," she said, but she maintained that Bo wasn't to blame for what happened.
AGELESS 'DYNASTY' STAR LINDA EVANS SHARES PLANS FOR 2025 IN INSPIRING NEW YEAR'S MESSAGE
"She didn’t break up my marriage," she insisted. "She did not go after him. He went after her."
Yvonne De Carlo, Charlton Heston and John Derek appear in a scene from "The Ten Commandments." (Getty Images)
THR wrote that Evans "doesn't hold much resentment for John, either," with the actress saying, "When he loved you, he was consumed with you."
She later added, "It was a favor they both did to me, because I ended up having an extraordinary life going off on my own."
And Bo, as she said, went on to have a long relationship with John that ended when he died in 1998.
John Derek and Bo Derek are interviewed by Barbara Walters in 1980. (ABC)

In a 1980 interview with The Washington Post, John said, "I had everything I wanted in Linda, so why I became interested in Bo, I don't know. At that time, she couldn't hold a candle to Linda, but something about her got me involved. She's an interesting girl, Bo is."
BO DEREK REVEALS WHY SHE FELT LIKE AN 'IMPOSTOR' AND WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD DESPITE BLOCKBUSTER FAME

He said at the time that he was on good terms with Evans, and that she was the one who researched the legalities of returning to the U.S. with Bo. After wrapping up the film in Greece, they stayed in Germany for some time, because, as he explained, "In the United States you have statutory rape and the Mann Act to contend with."
John and Bo Derek pose together in Qatar March 23, 1996. (Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images)
"It was definitely more acceptable there," Bo admitted to The Hollywood Reporter.
They were married in Las Vegas in 1976, and, three years later, "10" was released, and Bo became an international sex symbol.

However, she wasn't quite sure she was cut out for the job.

"I remember sobbing and saying, ‘I’m so confused. I don’t know what to do,’" Bo told THR. "And my husband said, ‘Well, do what you want. Just because everybody would kill for this career doesn’t mean you have to love it.’"
Bo Derek walks along the beach in swimwear as Samantha Taylor in the 1979 movie "10," directed by Blake Edwards. (Bettmann Archive)

She recalled telling him, "I just want to go make little films like we were doing before," referring to "Fantasies," which was finally released in 1981. She then starred in "Tarzan, The Ape Man," which John directed, and a couple other films helmed by her husband.
Since then, she's done smaller roles here and there, saying, "I didn’t always make the right career moves. But God, it was fun."

In 2002, four years after John's death, she was set up on a date with actor John Corbett, known for his roles in "Sex and the City" and "My Big Fat Greek Wedding."
Corbett had been given a list of names by a mutual friend and told to list his top five choices for a date, and he sent the list back with only Bo's name circled, saying, "It’s Bo or nobody."
John Corbett and Bo Derek in 2002 at the Oscars party where they had their first date and in 2026. (Sebastian Artz/Getty Images; Vivien Killilea/Getty Images for the Shania Twain Foundation)
The two hit it off, and as Corbett told The Hollywood Reporter, "We’ve kind of never been apart since then, really."

Bo married John in 2020, and when she was asked why they've worked so well together, she answered, "I fall in love. I fall hard, and I think that when someone else truly loves you, it’s such a gift to cherish. It’s kind of a miracle with all the billions of people in the world, so I cherish it."

title: Chuck Norris’ ‘Firewalker’ co-star doesn’t regret quitting Hollywood: ‘I’m glad I’m out of it’
summary: Melody Anderson, the "Flash Gordon" star who shared the screen with Chuck Norris, reveals why she quit acting to become a therapist helping families heal.
story: Fox News' Carley Shimkus provides details after Chuck Norris' family released a statement on the American legend's death.
Melody Anderson knew when it was time to say goodbye to Hollywood.
The "Flash Gordon" star, who once shared the screen with Chuck Norris, grew tired of the uncertainty of showbiz and the constant pressure to land her next role.
So, she traded acting for a new calling: helping families as a therapist.
And she hasn't looked back.
DAVID CHARVET ADMITS HE WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD AFTER 'BAYWATCH' TO FOCUS ON FATHERHOOD
"Firewalker," which starred Louis Gossett Jr., Melody Anderson and Chuck Norris, premiered Nov. 21, 1986. (TCD/Prod.DB/Alamy)
"I saw the writing on the wall," the former actress, who is marking the 40th anniversary of her Norris action-adventure comedy "Firewalker," told Fox News Digital.

"Part of it was aging out," she explained. "There was also the financial insecurity of always having to wait for a job. I thought, 'I've got to start organizing my life by the time I got into my mid-30s because I realized this is not something I can count on unless I win the lottery.' I still haven't. I still buy tickets, though.
Melody Anderson and Sam J. Jones appear in a scene from the movie "Flash Gordon." (Alamy)

"It wasn't really that scary for me to make that decision," Anderson continued. "The work was getting slower. My brain was getting duller. I wanted to pursue a career that would keep me growing. The curiosity and desire to learn keeps me young."
WATCH: CHUCK NORRIS DEAD AT 86

"Do I miss Hollywood? I miss being on the set. The crew was always so great. I loved the creative energy. I loved acting. But the actual business? I'm glad I'm out of it. I don't miss the business at all. There's always the anxiety of, 'When will my next job come in? Will it come in time so I can pay my mortgage?' All that extra stress becomes more intense as you get older in the business.
"I am so glad I don't have to deal with that anymore."
"Flash Gordon" (1980) is widely regarded as a cult classic. Although the sci-fi adventure received mixed reviews upon its release, it developed a devoted following over the years. (Getty Images)
Anderson stopped acting in 1995. Today, she is a licensed clinical social worker and therapist who specializes in addiction and recovery, trauma treatment and family therapy.
Actress Melody Anderson attends the West Coast premiere of "Life After Flash" at 2018 Beyond Fest at the Egyptian Theatre Oct. 3, 2018, in Hollywood, Calif. (Getty Images)

"When you're on a set, you hear a lot of stories from people," Anderson said. "I loved listening to people, hearing about their triumphs and struggles. I remember someone told me, 'You're pretty good at this. Have you ever thought about going back to school and getting a master's degree in social work?'
"I thought, 'Never.' But it really spoke to me. That's when I started working at a treatment center in New York and taking courses. I learned I loved family therapy.
Jeff Goldblum as Ernie Kovacs and Melody Anderson as Edie Adams appear in the ABC TV movie "Ernie Kovacs: Between the Laughter." (ABC)
"One of the reasons I love this career is because you can get really old, fat and wrinkled, and you can still help people," she said.

"I've been doing this for over 30 years now, and it's just so rewarding. I work with my clients to help them find peace and some healing. It's a wonderful life to live. On my deathbed, I'll know I did a good job, not for being the greatest actress, but for wanting to help others find peace."
Melody Anderson, circa the 1980s. (MediaPunch via Getty Images)
Still, Anderson has fond memories of her time in Hollywood, especially working opposite Norris. The actor died March 19, 2026, at 86.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Iconic martial artist and actor Chuck Norris died March 19, 2026, at the age of 86. (Gilbert Carrasquillo/Getty Images)

"Chuck loved doing tricks on set," she said with a laugh. "He loved to tease me. I remember he had this fake poop thing, and he put it right by my chair. But I immediately identified that it was from him because I'm also a prankster. I love spiders and bugs so it takes a lot to spook me. I just thought, 'Oh my God, he thinks I'm going to fall for this?'
Chuck Norris loved doing pranks on co-star Melody Anderson. (Jeff Kravitz/FilmMagic, Inc)

"I thought, 'I'm going to tell him this is stupid,'" she recalled. "But then he was going to punish me with an even greater prank. I wanted to make sure he never knew there would be a day when I would come and get him. I was going to get back at Chuck Norris. And he wouldn't suspect a thing."
During a break from filming, Anderson came across a wooden sculpture at a local market. She had an idea.
Melody Anderson and Chuck Norris appear in a scene from the 1986 movie "Firewalker." The two were known pranksters on set. (Alamy)

"I remember telling him that I had found the most beautiful sculpture I've ever seen," Anderson said. "Its head was loose. So, I showed it to him with so much pride. Of course, he grabs it and the head falls off. I pretended to cry. He felt horrible.

"And just when he started to feel really bad, I smiled at him. I told him, 'If you want to do pranks on me, be prepared. I'm better than you.' We had a good laugh about it. He was a huge prankster with a big sense of humor. I think that's why he wanted to do a comedy. And he did such a good job at it."
But Norris' fitness routine was no laughing matter.
Chuck Norris lifts weights in New York City, circa April 1993. (Getty Images)

"He really showed me how to ride a bike for exercise," Anderson said with a smile. "He told me the faster I go, the better it will be, because it will get my heart pumping. It will also build up my thighs without bulking them up. It helped me lose weight quickly. We had a ball working out together.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
President George H.W. Bush jogs with actor Chuck Norris and his son Michael Norris at the U.S. Naval Observatory in Washington on March 21, 1990. (AFP via Getty Images)

"You have to remember, he was in Korea," Anderson continued. "He was a veteran. He knew the importance of taking care of yourself, defending yourself. He had that discipline of always working out, staying in shape. He saw it as an art form, taking care of your body. He was so disciplined.
Chuck Norris and Lou Gossett Jr. attend the 16th annual Shelby Awards at the Beverly Hilton Hotel in Beverly Hills Dec. 4, 1986. (Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

"He would get up every morning and work out for an hour, sometimes an hour and a half. I wanted to learn from him, so I started waking up early to work out with Chuck. And I'm so grateful for it because now I know how to exercise properly."
But there was one time when trying to stay healthy backfired on Norris and co-star Louis Gossett Jr.

Despite its star power, "Firewalker" failed to win over most critics when it hit theaters in 1986. Roger Ebert gave it just one out of four stars. However, the Los Angeles Times offered a more favorable review, praising the movie's humor and Norris' willingness to embrace a lighter role. (Alamy)

"These were two very, very macho men," Anderson said with a laugh. "When they came to Mexico, they were just, 'I'm not going to get sick. No ice, no anything. We're only eating the hotel food.' My belief has always been that if you eat the food, you'll get over it quickly. So, I was eating off the taco carts right outside the studio. They kept warning me, 'You're going to get sick.'

Best known for his tough guy roles in action movies (seen here), Chuck Norris showed off his comedic chops in the 1986 action-adventure comedy "Firewalker," embracing a more playful side of his on-screen persona. (Cannon/Getty Images)
"Well, they both got sick — terribly sick. They were unable to work. And me? I was fine. I remember I approached them and said, 'How are we feeling now, boys? Want some more hotel food?'"
Forty years later, Anderson remembers Norris as more than the tough guy audiences saw on screen.

Melody Anderson stopped acting in 1995. (ABC)
"He was a very gregarious, happy guy," she said. "I miss him."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Ashton Kutcher on track for billionaire status after ignoring wife Mila Kunis' early tech warnings
summary: Ashton Kutcher's Sound Ventures saw its $435 million Anthropic investment grow to $7 billion after the AI company's stock market debut on Nov. 19.
story: Ashton Kutcher is on his way to becoming a billionaire after investing in tech despite Mila Kunis previously warning him not to. (Taylor Hill/FilmMagic)
Ashton Kutcher is on his way to becoming a billionaire after going against his wife's advice and investing his money in tech.

According to Newsweek, the 48-year-old actor's venture capital firm, Sound Ventures, made a $435 million investment in the artificial intelligence company, Anthropic, in 2023, an investment that is now worth $7 billion.
Bloomberg reports that the company owns 0.5 percent of Anthropic, which has an estimated IPO valuation of $1.4 trillion. Anthropic went public on the stock exchange Nov. 19.

Kutcher co-founded Sound Ventures in 2015 and, since then, has invested in a number of successful companies. He previously invested in Spotify, Uber and Airbnb with his investment firm, A-Grade Investments, which he co-founded in 2010.
Ashton Kutcher is on his way to becoming a billionaire after investing in tech despite Mila Kunis previously warning him not to. (Taylor Hill/FilmMagic)
WHO IS DARIO AMODEI, THE ANTHROPIC CEO PUSHING INDEPENDENT AI OVERSIGHT?
Kutcher has since relinquished his position as partner at Sound Ventures but has stayed on as a senior advisor.
Although the "Two and a Half Men" actor has found success with his investments, his wife, actress Mila Kunis, wasn't always on board with him investing in certain companies.

"Early in our dating, two things came up. He was like, ‘Hey, there’s this company, it’s kind of a rideshare,'" she said on "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert Show" in 2021, referencing his investment in Uber.
"He’s like, ‘There’s this company, it’s kind of like a cab company, but anyone can drive the cab.’ I was like, ‘That's the worst idea ever.'"
Anthropic went public on the stock exchange Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The actor decided to convince Kunis by suggesting she try the service herself, an idea that left her "furious."

"He is, like, ‘Let me get you this thing, called Uber, let me order it, you can test it out,’" she said. "And I was like, 'You are going to put me in a car with a stranger. What is wrong with you? Like, I was furious at him."

He later approached her about investing in Bitcoin, saying he told her, "I gotta explain this thing to you, tell me if I’m crazy," and then he told her about "this thing, mining for money. It’s called cryptocurrency."
Kunis told Kutcher not to invest in Uber or Bitcoin, thinking they weren't going to be successful. (Taylor Hill/WireImage)
"I was like, ‘Then who is going to make sure it’s safe?’ He was like, ‘That’s the point,'" she said. "He didn’t listen to me. ... This happens all the time."

When speaking with Business Insider in April 2017, Kutcher admitted he initially passed on Uber when the CEO of the company approached him but then realized "there was a product market fit there" and immediately called the CEO back.
He also admitted to having the same feelings about Airbnb, noting his initial thought was, "Who's going to want a stranger sleeping on their couch?"
Kutcher was unsure about investing in Airbnb and Uber in the beginning. (Kate Green/Getty Images)

"Oftentimes, the foundation of great companies are extraordinarily counterintuitive where the founders have some data nodes that would suggest that the intuition relative to a certain sector is wrong or that there's some fundamental intuition that is wrong," he explained.

"And that we when you unveil that fundamental intuition to be wrong, you actually find an entire pasture of green grass that nobody else is building in because there's a fundamental intuition … that has been an assumption of so many people for so long that they've never actually built into that sector."

During her interview with Stephen Colbert, Kunis said it is not uncommon for her husband to approach her with a "ludicrous" idea, but somehow he is always right.
Kunis joked that she's never been happier to be wrong. (Todd Owyoung/NBC via Getty Images)

"There are companies all the time that he will talk about that, to me, seem so ludicrous," she said. "Why would I want to sleep on someone's couch and pay for it? Like, it is ludicrous, and yet here we are. And I Airbnb everything and Uber everywhere, and I use cryptocurrency. So, guess what? I have never been happier to be wrong."

Kutcher and Kunis first met when they were both cast on "That '70s Show" when he was 20 years old and she was 14. Although they played love interests on the show, their real-life friendship never crossed the line into romance at the time.
Kunis and Kutcher met when they were both cast on "That '70s Show." (FOX Image Collection via Getty Images)

They began dating in April 2012 after they reconnected at the Golden Globe Awards in January 2012. Kutcher was married to Demi Moore from 2005 to 2011, while Kunis was in a long-term relationship with Macaulay Culkin from 2002 to 2011.

"The people that we were back then would never be together. But it's just such a bummer that we missed out on 20 years together. I look back, and I think, ‘We could have spent 20 years together,’" Kunis said on the "WTF with Marc Maron" podcast in July 2018.
"But we would have never been together if we didn't both go what we went through in order to be the people that we were when we met."

The couple reconnected at the Golden Globes in 2012 and tied the knot in 2015. (Taylor Hill/Getty Images)
The two got engaged in February 2014 and got married in July 2015. During their relationship, they have welcomed two children together: Wyatt, 12, and Dimitri, 9.

"Her talents, her skills, her gifts," he said. "But I knew that she didn't need me. And she knew that I didn't need her."

title: Meghan Markle’s brand gets Oprah push, but expert says duchess still has ‘a credibility problem’
summary: Oprah Winfrey's "Favorite Things" list features Meghan Markle's As Ever gift basket, but experts say the duchess still faces a "credibility problem."
story: Dan Wakeford, founder of Celebrity Intelligence, says Meghan Markle could reset her career by finding an extraordinary script and returning to the acting roots that made her famous.
Meghan Markle may have Oprah Winfrey's stamp of approval, but experts say even the queen of daytime television can't guarantee the Duchess of Sussex something money can't buy: credibility.
Winfrey's "Favorite Things" list for 2026 debuted Nov. 12, and Meghan's As Ever The Signature Basket landed a spot.
But while Winfrey's endorsement could help Meghan sell her products, experts say winning over the public may prove a much tougher challenge.
MEGHAN MARKLE'S FAILED MARTHA STEWART DREAMS MOCKED BY COMEDIAN: 'SHE WAS SLINGING JAM'
Meghan Markle still has a "credibility problem" despite Oprah Winfrey's push, experts told Fox News Digital. (Netflix)

"Meghan doesn't have a name recognition problem," royal expert Kinsey Schofield, the host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital. "She has a credibility problem, in my opinion.
"Oprah has spent decades convincing Americans that her recommendations are worth their money. Meghan is benefiting from that trust.

"But I also think Oprah's association with the Sussexes has come at a reputational cost. Her 2021 interview attracted criticism for its lack of challenging follow-up questions. Oprah's endorsement may generate sales, but I don't think either woman automatically improves the other's credibility anymore."

Meghan launched As Ever in 2025 as a rebranding of her earlier concept, American Riviera Orchard, marking the Duchess of Sussex's return to the lifestyle space she once occupied with her pre-royal blog, "The Tig."

The brand debuted with a tight, curated collection of small-batch essentials, including raspberry spreads, wildflower honey with honeycomb, crêpe and shortbread cookie mixes, flower sprinkles and herbal teas, which famously sold out within an hour of going live.
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE FEEDING THE 'PUBLICITY MACHINE' DESPITE PRIVACY DEMANDS: EXPERT
Oprah Winfrey put Meghan Markle's signature gift basket on her coveted "Favorite Things" list. (Lanna Apisukh/WWD via Getty Images)
As Ever has since expanded beyond kitchen staples into seasonal drops featuring Napa Valley wines, scented candles and curated holiday gift hampers.
Winfrey's addition of Meghan's gift basket on her Favorite Things list will drive brand awareness and sales heading into the holiday season, according to British royal expert Hilary Fordwich.
Meghan Markle became the Duchess of Sussex when she married Prince Harry in 2018. (Ben Stansall/WPA Pool/Getty Images)

"This celebrity lifestyle brand arena is such a frightfully crowded space, so such a high-profile celebrity endorsement certainly is a welcome differentiator," she added. "Yet Oprah does feature many products, including from other famous friends."
The business venture remains the centerpiece of Meghan's post-royal business strategy, blending her California aesthetic with direct-to-consumer retail.

Meghan Markle's spread in keepsake packaging sold for $14. (As Ever)
Meghan's brand wouldn't have the same star power, however, without Winfrey's push, brand expert Doug Eldridge told Fox News Digital.
"Would Markle have the mic if she never married Prince Harry? No. She was the fourth lead on a short-lived legal drama on the USA Network," the founder of Achilles PR explained.

"Would Markle have the sizzle if she wasn’t in the royal spotlight? No. Hence, the tell-all books and manufactured drama to remain in the conversation, even after her unofficial exile from royal duties. Would As Ever be conversationally relevant were it not created by an erstwhile Duchess and promoted by the Queen of American TV? No.
Meghan Markle worked alongside Patrick J. Adams on "Suits" for seven years. (Shane Mahood/USA Network/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
"Objectively speaking, it’s an overpriced line of basic household goods hitting the U.S. market at a time of inflation, spiking gas prices and overall economic uncertainty," Eldridge added.

"That said, seemingly every celebrity these days has their own brand of tequila, wine or hard seltzer brand. The shelf life for celebrity influence is fleeting, so most of these personalities are branching out (and cashing in) while they still can."
Meghan Markle sold the As Ever jar of honey for $28. (As Ever)

However, Winfrey endorsing Meghan's product for a second time is "highly significant," according to one royal expert.

"As its sales and profits are undisclosed, we cannot know how successful it actually is. Because it is linked to Meghan, it has been the subject of enormous speculation, but we don’t know turnover, costs and profit, if any."

While critics question whether Winfrey's endorsement can boost Meghan's credibility or ensure As Ever's long-term success, others say the media mogul's continued support proves the duchess still has powerful allies and influence in Hollywood.

title: Jackson 5 icon Marlon Jackson, 69, goes public with Stage 4 cancer battle months after onstage fall
summary: Marlon Jackson, 69, says he's privately fought Stage 4 prostate cancer for four years, undergoing surgery and radiation while leaning on faith and prayer.
story: Victoria Price told Fox News Digital that as long as there is Halloween, people will listen to the horror icon's narration in the hit song.
Months after sparking fan concern with a frightening onstage fall, Jackson 5 icon Marlon Jackson disclosed that he has been privately battling cancer for the past four years.
"And I'm going to tell people right now, God has me," he insisted during an appearance on "The Farah Shammas Podcast." "He already told me he has me. I've had cancer for four years.
"But I'm great. I'm good," Jackson, 69, added. "Bad grass don't die. So, I'm going to be around for a long time."
LIFE OF MICHAEL JACKSON: THE KING OF POP FROM HIS START WITH JACKSON 5, MASSIVE SOLO HITS, HIS SCANDALS
Marlon Jackson shared his cancer diagnosis during a new interview. (Mike Lewis Photography/Redferns)
Jackson explained that his road to recovery required both aggressive medical intervention and major lifestyle changes.
"I've already had my prostate gland removed, and I've had radiation treatment and everything is fine," the Jackson 5 member said. "Everything is great. I walk almost four miles, four times a week."
His lifestyle changes also included a change to his diet.

Marlon Jackson, seen with the Jackson 5, also spoke about how he's been handling treatment. (Fin Costello/Redferns)
"Well, I stopped eating beef and pork in 1977 and, after the cancer, I did do away with sugar and careful what I put in my body and try to take care of myself," Jackson explained.
While adjusting his diet and exercise habits, Jackson maintained that his faith and the prayers of others have carried him through his recovery.
"I'm doing great, so I thank everybody who have prayed for me. The Lord told me, you know, cast your burdens on him, and he'll take care of them and that's what he's done, so I can't complain."

title: Darius Rucker says he used to drink a bottle of whiskey a day during wild Hootie & the Blowfish years
summary: Darius Rucker admits drinking a bottle of whiskey a day on the road as Hootie & the Blowfish fame fueled substance abuse in new Hulu documentary.
story: Hootie & the Blowfish singer Darius Rucker dedicated new record to mother Carolyn.
Darius Rucker's meteoric rise to fame as the lead singer of Hootie & the Blowfish was captured in the latest Hulu documentary, "They Called Me Hootie."

Breaking onto the scene in the early '90s, the group of college friends from South Carolina broke records with "Cracked Rear View" released in 1994, but fame and fortune came at a cost and Rucker soon spiraled into substance abuse and drinking issues at the peak of the band's popularity.
Rucker, 60, admitted that at one point he was drinking one bottle of whiskey per day while on the road, and casual drug use became routine.
BRAD PITT SAYS HE CAN DRINK IN ‘RESTRAINED MANNER’ AFTER 7 SOBER YEARS, BUT EXPERT RAISES RED FLAG
Darius Rucker was once depending on drugs and alcohol while touring with Hootie & the Blowfish. (Terry Wyatt/WireImage)
"I smoked a little pot," Rucker said. "If we had a day over, someone would get some acid." After the band upgraded to a tour bus, things took a drastic detour.
"One day, I came back to our bus, I walked in the back and two of the guys were lining up some cocaine," Rucker said. "And the party just was on from that point."
‘BACK TO THE FUTURE’ STAR CHRISTOPHER LLOYD CONFESSES HE WAS ‘HOOKED’ ON COCAINE DURING ‘TAXI’ YEARS
He added, "We earned our reputation. We went crazy, man. It was rock and roll."
Rucker recalled once buying trash bags full of mushrooms from someone on the bus.

"I'm like, 'Mushrooms? Really? How many mushrooms you got?' 'We've got two garbage bags of mushrooms,'" he said. "And he's like, 'Well, we're probably gonna make about $45,000.' It’s like, 'What if we give you [$30,000] right now?'
"I went and got T-shirt money and came back with two garbage bags that we kept in our freezers for two and a half years. I always said we never had a drug problem because we could always afford it."
Hootie & the Blowfish found massive success from their debut album, "Cracked Rear View." (Gie Knaeps)
Hootie & the Blowfish supported Darius Rucker at his star unveiling. (Kevin Winter)

Rucker became "instant friends" with Woody Harrelson after meeting backstage following a show, and the pair soon became smoking buddies. Harrelson guessed they had "maybe smoked about 100,000 joints together."
"What do you do when you smoke joints? You just sit and talk. I just loved listening to him spin a yarn," Harrelson said.
COUNTRY SINGER RUSTON KELLY COMMITS TO SOBRIETY AFTER RELAPSING ON DRUGS FOLLOWING FREAK GOLF CART CRASH
At one point, bandmate Mark Bryan remembered when Rucker's penchant for rock 'n' roll impacted the band after he took ecstasy before a gig in London.

"He decided to, like, start exploring the theater during the show," Bryan said. "It felt to me like we were losing the crowd, which is the worst feeling at any time at any show. He probably didn’t feel that way. He probably thought he was taking things to the next level. "
Rucker admitted a girl at the show gave him the drugs, but didn't know why he took it, and said he "could've waited till the show was over, but, you know, I just took it."
Darius Rucker and Woody Harrelson became friends after meeting backstage following a Hootie & the Blowfish show. (KMazur)
"We went on the stage and I was introducing songs we weren’t playing," Rucker said before Bryan explained they had a "huge fight" backstage.
"I headbutted a cinderblock wall," he said. "I’ll never forget doing that. We were not on the same page in that moment."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
While Rucker's life on the road was bumpy, his wife back home was having an equally difficult time with Rucker's touring habits.
"She said that I could straighten up and we would be happy, or I could keep living that life and she'll figure out how she can make me miserable," Rucker recalled.
Hootie & the Blowfish toured in support of the 30th anniversary of "Cracked Rear View" in 2024. (Daniel Knighton/Getty Images)
"The day before she said that was the last day I partied like that. The next day I called and said I need my own bus."
While taking a break from the band, Rucker visited Harrelson's Hawaiian home, where the singer had the "two best weeks" of his life before tragedy nearly struck.
"We had a blast. We did naked yoga, and I ate so pure and vegan," Rucker remembered.
While walking on the cliffs one day, Harrelson asked if Rucker could swim, and told him if he jumped in, he'd have to navigate a strong rip current.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
"I dive out, and I open my eyes and look both ways, and I realize, there's no beach and all I see is fish," Rucker said. "And I come up and I start to swim out and I'm caught."
Harrelson admitted the water was "a little rugged that day and he probably shouldn't have gone in."
The members of Hootie & the Blowfish met in college in South Carolina. (Paul Natkin)

"It seemed like forever that we were out there trying to get out," Rucker remembered. "I had gotten myself to a peace. I had accepted that God had given me this amazing life that is exactly what I asked for, and if it had to end right there, then when I got to heaven I was going to say thank you."
"He looked at me, and it was just like Woody from 'Cheers,' he looked at me and giggled and said ‘not on my watch.’"
"I wasn't going to let that happen," Harrelson said before Rucker chimed in that it was "surreal. Woody Harrelson had really literally just saved my life."
The band celebrated the 30th anniversary of their massively successful album "Cracked Rear View" in 2024.

With tracks including "Only Wanna Be With You," "Hold My Hand" and "Let Her Cry," the debut catalog for the band from South Carolina was released in July 1994 and has been certified platinum 21 times over.
Rucker has two children with his ex-wife, Beth Leonard, and one daughter with Elizabeth Ann Phillips. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images)
Hootie & the Blowfish went on to release four more studio albums before going on hiatus in 2008, leading Rucker to pursue an entirely different genre: country music.
In 2023, Rucker released his eighth solo album, "Carolyn's Boy," a tribute to his late mother who died in 1992 just as Hootie was picking up steam.
Rucker noted that his biggest disappointment was that his mother never got a chance to see his success.
"At first it was really hard to accept, I mean it was so out of the blue," he said of his mother's death.

"To know that she didn't get to see me do what I told her I was going to do since I was five-years-old. She never got to sit on the phone talking to her girlfriends about me being on David Letterman tonight and how she was going to stay up even though she had to work early tomorrow ... and how she never got to do that is still heartbreaking."

title: 'I Play Rocky' star Anthony Ippolito packed on weight with 'entire lifestyle shift' to play Sylvester Stallone
summary: Anthony Ippolito gained more than 30 pounds and trained in a boxing gym to transform into Sylvester Stallone's Rocky Balboa for Peter Farrelly's biopic.
story: Anthony Ippolito told Fox News Digital that he endured an "entire lifestyle" change to portray Sylvester Stallone in "I Play Rocky."
Anthony Ippolito's transformation into Sylvester Stallone for "I Play Rocky" didn't happen overnight.
Ippolito, 27, packed on the pounds and overhauled his diet to portray the heavyweight boxer in the Peter Farrelly-directed biopic about the making of the Academy Award-winning film, "Rocky."

The New York native explained how he endured "an entire lifestyle shift" before jumping in front of the camera to film "I Play Rocky," which follows Stallone's pursuit to bring Rocky Balboa to life on the big screen — a movie Stallone not only wrote in a few days as a struggling actor, but also refused to sell to a major studio unless he played the starring role.
JOHN MADDEN ROLE PUSHES NICOLAS CAGE TO DRAMATIC PHYSICAL TRANSFORMATION WITH ‘BRUTAL’ DIET, PROSTHETICS
AnnaSophia Robb starred as Sylvester Stallone's first wife, Sasha Czack. (Claire Folger/ 2026 Amazon Content Services LLC.)

"I had to gain a bunch of weight," Ippolito told Fox News Digital of his incredible transformation to play the boxer, which included the main priority of "eating a ton of food" every day before focusing on his actual diet and training.

"So, because knowing Stallone was playing Rocky, who is a heavyweight boxer in the movie, and he was a huge fan of Steve Reeves growing up," Ippolito explained of his preparation for becoming Rocky Balboa.
SYLVESTER STALLONE CALLS HIMSELF AN 'IDIOT' FOR DOING HIS OWN STUNTS, DETAILS NINE BACK SURGERIES

Reeves was known for enduring multiple full-body workouts per week to not only create, but also maintain his fighting physique, and prior to starring in the '58 Italian classic "Hercules," Reeves was credited with bringing bodybuilding to a global level as Mr. America in 1947, followed by Mr. Universe in 1950.
Sylvester Stallone wrote "Rocky" and starred as boxer Rocky Balboa. (Getty Images)
Anthony Ippolito trained for months to become Sylvester Stallone in "I Play Rocky." (Claire Folger/2026 Amazon Content Services LLC.)
Ippolito gained more than 30 pounds and spent months weightlifting and training in a boxing gym while also learning Stallone's specific dialect to transform into Rocky Balboa.
"Stallone started weightlifting at a really young age, so he always had some type of physique," Ippolito said.

"It's something that's a really recognizable part of 'Rocky,' and I kind of knew I had to be there, so it was an entire lifestyle shift, to be honest with you."

Ippolito's transformation completely astounded the Academy Award winner, who admitted that he had "mixed" feelings about the film but was ultimately blown away by his character.
Anthony Ippolito stars as Sylvester Stallone in "I Play Rocky." (Claire Folger/2026 Amazon Content Services LLC.)
Sylvester Stallone filmed "Rocky" by the Schuylkill River in Fairmount Park, Philadelphia, with the old Pennsylvania Railroad Bridge in the background. (Silver Screen Collection)

While promoting his memoir, "The Steps," earlier this year, The Hollywood Reporter noted how Stallone grappled with the idea of the biopic and was initially "kind of mixed because I'm going, 'I’m not dead yet. Aren’t we jumping the gun a little bit?'"
"And then I saw this video of this kid [Ippolito]. I actually thought it was me the first moment; there were a couple of angles. I go to my daughter and say, 'That’s unbelievable.'"

Written by Peter Gamble and directed by Peter Farrelly, "I Play Rocky" followed Sylvester Stallone's quest to bring Rocky Balboa to the big screen. (Claire Folger/2026 Amazon Content Services LLC.)
"It's just, it's kind of incredible. And so hearing him say that is really, really, really cool."

"I Play Rocky" follows Stallone's quest to not only write a marketable film for a movie studio, but also his own pursuit in refusing to sell his words unless he was the actor reciting the script.

title: Who owns your body parts after surgery? Doctors uncover the complicated rules
summary: Surgical patients are asking hospitals to hand over removed organs, teeth and joints as keepsakes, but pathology rules and release forms stand in the way.
story: Dr. Raymond Lynch, director of the Division of Transplantation at HRSA, discusses how updated federal organ donation guidelines seek to protect patients and improve communication with families facing difficult end-of-life decisions.
Most people want to forget their time in the operating room, yet some surgical patients insist on bringing their removed body parts home as souvenirs.

While hospitals usually throw away removed tissue as medical waste, a small number of patients asks doctors to pack up their organs, teeth and worn-out joints after surgery, according to TIME magazine.
Doctors say these patients want keepsakes for many reasons, from marking personal milestones to honoring cultural traditions.
ORGAN HARVESTING BEGAN WHILE PATIENTS STILL SHOWED ‘SIGNS OF LIFE,’ FEDERAL INVESTIGATION FINDS

Examples included a patient who kept her removed uterus in a jar after a hysterectomy as a reminder of the pain she survived, and another who dried her removed fallopian tubes to display in a box with flowers, according to the report.
While hospitals typically discard removed tissue as medical waste, some surgical patients ask to bring their organs, teeth or joints home as souvenirs. (iStock)
Other saved items included a pulled wisdom tooth fashioned into a calligraphy pen and a piece of medical tubing saved from a hospital stay and later given to a future spouse, the magazine said.

Dr. Robyn Power, a gynecologic surgeon in South Florida, told TIME that only about five of her patients finished the paperwork to take tissue home over the past year, though more people are asking about it.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
She said patients living with painful conditions like endometriosis sometimes want the removed tissue as physical proof of what disrupted their lives.
"It means something different to everybody," Power said.
Hospital rules and safety

Taking a body part home takes more than asking a surgeon in the recovery room.Dr. Kenneth Perry, an emergency room physician based in South Carolina, told Fox News Digital that rules surrounding who owns removed tissue vary widely.
Before any surgical tissue can be released to a patient, pathologists must examine the specimen for disease. (iStock)

"As odd as it sounds, the ownership of tissue and other things removed from a person’s body is actually not settled law," Perry said. "Each state and each institution will have its own views on how to handle different tissues."
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

In the emergency room, Perry said doctors often let patients take home low-risk items like passed kidney stones, salivary gland stones or splinters, as long as the objects are not tied to a police case, like a bullet.
Larger organs or body parts carry more risk because doctors must rule out infection or serious disease before releasing them.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
"For instance, if an extremity or an organ has been removed due to infection or bleeding, it is often required that it goes through pathology testing to ensure it is safe," Perry said.

He added that for pregnancy-related tissues, such as a placenta or remains from a miscarriage, hospitals typically have different rules and separate steps involved for families who ask to take them home.
Patients debate the rules online
Some surgical patients have taken to Reddit to share their confusion and experiences with trying to keep removed body parts.
Surgeons say patients request removed tissue for varied reasons, from honoring cultural traditions to keeping physical proof of chronic conditions. (iStock)

"Seeing as the hip bone is coming from my own body, I don't understand why I cannot," one user wrote ahead of a hip replacement in Washington State after a surgeon claimed that state law rejected his request to keep the bone.
"My best friend's son got to keep one of his tonsils to take to school for show and tell," the user added.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
Others pushed back, pointing to health hazards and hospital rules.
"It's considered medical waste. Yes, bones can carry risks," one commenter wrote.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"It really depends on the state laws, but most will not allow it," wrote another user who said they worked in pathology. "You can have a funeral home bury it if you like, but probably not take it home."

title: Popular bedroom supplements often fail to deliver, says longevity physician
summary: Dr. Pablo Prichard shares why most sexual enhancement supplements fail and how L-arginine and L-citrulline may help blood flow and erectile dysfunction.
story: Dr. Pablo Prichard, an Arizona-based surgeon who focuses on longevity and preventative health, warns that most over-the-counter sexual enhancement products are ineffective — and some carry health risks.

Pharmacy aisles and social media feeds are crowded with capsules, powders and gummies promising to boost libido and sexual performance. Yet according to physicians and clinical research, most over-the-counter sexual enhancement products are ineffective — and some carry health risks.
It's a mistake to treat all sexual health concerns as a single problem, according to Dr. Pablo Prichard, an Arizona-based surgeon who focuses on longevity and preventative health.
Before reaching for a bottle, patients should understand the difference between low sex drive and physical performance issues like erectile dysfunction or vaginal dryness, he told Fox News Digital.
WHY STACKING SUPPLEMENTS WITHOUT A BLOOD TEST FIRST CAN DO MORE HARM THAN GOOD
"When you're looking at supplements, you have to think, ‘Is this supplement affecting what my problem is individually?’" Prichard said.
"Because if you have a hormonal issue, and you take a supplement that supposedly increases your blood flow, that doesn't necessarily improve your condition."
Hundreds of unregulated "all-natural" supplements have been found by the FDA to contain hidden, undeclared prescription drugs like sildenafil and tadalafil, the doctor said. (iStock)

If performance issues stem from restricted circulation, certain amino acids may offer modest support. Supplements like L-arginine and L-citrulline target the nitric oxide pathway, which helps relax and widen blood vessels, Prichard said.
According to Cleveland Clinic, L-citrulline converts into L-arginine in the body to boost nitric oxide production, and small clinical studies suggest it may help improve mild erectile dysfunction.
VIAGRA COULD DO MORE THAN ADVERTISED AS STUDY REVEALS SURPRISING HEALTH SUPERPOWER
Still, the clinic notes that overall scientific evidence remains mixed, larger clinical trials are needed, and the supplements are less reliable than prescription treatments.

"If you actually have a blood-flow issue, then taking a supplement like this … that improves your blood flow could actually help," Prichard said. "If you don't have a blood-flow issue, and it's another problem, then taking a supplement like this probably won't help."
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

While certain herbal extracts, such as Panax ginseng and saffron, have shown potential in small trials to improve erectile function and sexual satisfaction, experts urge caution with unregulated sexual enhancement blends.
"The FDA has repeatedly seen actual Viagra in these 'herbal Viagra' medications," Prichard said.

Mixing hidden prescription ingredients or certain herbs with heart medications, blood pressure drugs or blood thinners can trigger life-threatening drops in blood pressure or elevated bleeding risks. (iStock)

Laboratory testing by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has identified hundreds of over-the-counter products marketed as "all-natural" sexual enhancers that secretly contain prescription drug ingredients — most commonly sildenafil (the active ingredient in Viagra) and tadalafil (found in Cialis).

Because these hidden drugs aren't listed on the label, the agency warns that consumers risk dangerous side effects or severe drops in blood pressure, particularly if they take heart medications containing nitrates.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Taking unknown doses of prescription erectile dysfunction drugs can trigger dangerous side effects.

Prichard warned that combining hidden sildenafil — or even high doses of L-arginine — with heart medications like nitroglycerin or hypertension drugs can cause life-threatening drops in blood pressure. Similarly, mixing herbs like ginkgo biloba with blood thinners can elevate bleeding risks.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
For both men and women experiencing low desire or dryness tied to shifting hormone levels, consulting with a physician is more effective than guessing at the store, the doctor advised.

Fundamental lifestyle habits such as getting enough sleep, exercising regularly, managing stress and consulting a doctor for underlying medical conditions are far more effective than relying on pills. (iStock)
Any new or worsening changes in sexual function warrant a medical checkup, as they could be a warning sign of cardiovascular disease, diabetes or depression.
"I think a lot of times, people take the easy way out and say, 'Yeah, I have this problem, I'm just going to take this pill ... and that's going to fix my problem,'" Prichard said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Foundational habits like prioritizing sleep, managing stress and getting both aerobic and strength exercise "can have a much bigger influence on your sexual health than just taking a supplement," the doctor added.
Khloe Quill is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital. She and the lifestyle team cover a range of story topics including food and drink, travel, and health.

title: Common sleep habit linked to 50% higher death risk in heart patients, recent study finds
summary: A PLOS One study of 3,287 US adults with heart disease links sleeping nine or more hours to a 51% higher risk of all-cause mortality over 15 years.
story: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel discusses a new study challenging the traditional eight hour sleep rule on America Reports.

Adults with heart disease who sleep nine or more hours per night could be at a higher risk of death from both heart-related and non-heart-related causes than those who sleep seven to eight hours, according to a recent study.

The cohort study in the journal PLOS One, titled "Sleep duration and cause-specific mortality among US adults with heart disease," analyzed data from 3,287 adults with heart disease from the 2004 National Health Survey linked to the National Death Index running until Dec. 31, 2019.

In the National Health Survey, participants answered whether they had heart disease based on if they had ever been told they had coronary heart disease, a heart attack or a heart condition or disease, according to the study.
MORE NAPS, HIGHER RISK? RESEARCH LINKS DAYTIME SLEEP TO HEALTH WARNINGS IN AGING ADULTS

"Sleep affects blood pressure, blood sugar regulation, inflammation, and appetite hormones, and all of these influence cardiovascular risk," Erin Palinksi-Wade, a New Jersey-based registered dietitian and Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist (CDCES), told Fox News Digital.
Sleeping too much or not enough could be warning signs of various health problems and worth mentioning to a doctor. (iStock)
The study authors adjusted for health factors and lifestyle behaviors such as body mass index (BMI), alcohol consumption, smoking, physical activity, diabetes, hypertension and more.
Sleep per 24 hours was categorized into durations of six hours or less, seven to eight hours and nine or more hours.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER
Over approximately 15 years of follow-up, 49.4% of participants died.
Out of all participants, 16.7% died from heart-related causes and 32.6% died from non-heart-related causes.
Sleep impacts blood pressure, blood sugar regulation and inflammation, which all influence cardiovascular risk. (iStock)
After adjusting for all lifestyle factors, researchers found that sleeping nine or more hours was linked to a higher mortality risk, compared with sleeping seven to eight hours.
There was a 51% increased risk of all causes of death, a 53% increased risk of heart-related causes of death and a 50% increased risk of non-heart-related mortality.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS
Sleep duration of six hours or less was significantly associated with non-heart-related death only in the least-adjusted model, and the connection weakened with further adjustment.

"Because the study is observational, it shows an association, not cause and effect. Long sleep may be a symptom of underlying problems like more advanced heart disease, depression, sleep apnea, or medication side effects, and the study couldn't fully account for those," Palinski-Wade said.
It's important to monitor heart health, which includes paying attention to sleep quality and quantity, registered dietitian Erin Palinski-Wade noted. (iStock)
The authors noted that their findings do not invalidate the negative cardiovascular effects of getting too little sleep.

"I'm not aware of a convincing biological mechanism by which extra hours of sleep damage the heart," Antony Chu, MD, a cardiologist and clinical assistant professor at Brown University’s Warren Alpert School of Medicine, told Fox News Digital.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"What I see clinically is that patients sleep longer because something is pulling on their reserve: worsening heart failure, untreated obstructive or central sleep apnea, depression, sedating medications, anemia or frailty," Chu said.

Sleeping too much or too little are both potential red flags, Palinski-Wade noted, so it’s important for people to pay attention to how rested they feel rather than only focusing on the number of hours they slept.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
Because the study only tested people with pre-existing heart conditions, it should not be used to suggest that prolonged sleep leads to heart disease in the general population, she added.
Sadie Chafe is a writer on the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

title: Social media users are eating huge amounts of carrots and shrimp for a natural tan
summary: Dr. Navin Arora says the viral carrot tan from eating carrots, tomatoes and shrimp is real but no substitute for sunscreen and basic sun safety.
story: Dermatologist Dr. Jody Levine joins 'Fox & Friends' to discuss critical sun safety topics during Wellness Week. Dr. Levine explains why a base tan offers minimal protection and compares different types of sunscreen and the protection they provide.
Some social media users are "carrotmaxxing," "tomatomaxxing" and "shrimpmaxxing," in the hopes of getting a sun-kissed glow that lasts them all winter long.

The trend, which calls for eating large quantities of carrots, tomatoes and shrimp, or taking supplements packed with their compounds, relies on carotenoids, natural pigments found in certain foods, the New York Post recently reported.

The outlet highlighted wellness creators promoting raw carrots as a way to get a "carrot tan," including one who said she no longer gets fake tans, and followed two Atlanta moms who said they take a daily carotenoid supplement for a "healthy glow."
COULD 'HUMANMAXXING' ACTUALLY HELP YOU LIVE LONGER? HERE'S WHAT EXPERTS SAY
The supplement they take is a blend of three carotenoid pigments: beta-carotene, lycopene and astaxanthin, the compounds that give carrots, tomatoes, shrimp and salmon their color.
Carrots contain beta-carotene, a pigment that can affect skin tone. (iStock)
Wellness influencer Lee Tilghman Pollis, meanwhile, recently said on Instagram that raw carrots have given her "the best skin of my life and I will die on this hill."

Another influencer went viral on TikTok for her carrot tan, telling followers that she no longer gets fake tans or stays out in the sun and instead eats three to four large carrots a day for several months to build up her tan.
DOCTOR REVEALS 4 HIDDEN HEALTH RISKS OF SPENDING TOO MUCH TIME INDOORS
Experts say the skin-color change is real and generally harmless, but it's no substitute for basic sun-safety measures.
Carotenoids in tomatoes, shrimp and salmon can also give foods their yellow, orange or red hues. (iStock)

"Beta-carotene, lycopene and astaxanthin are fat-soluble pigments, and when you eat a lot of them they build up in the outermost layer of the skin," Dr. Navin Arora, a board-certified dermatologist and medical director of Borealis Dermatology in New York, told Fox News Digital.
NEW CALIFORNIA LAW WILL RESTRICT SALES OF SOME MUSCLE-BUILDING SUPPLEMENTS TO MINORS
The buildup can create a yellow or orange tint, often first visible on the palms, soles and around the nose.

There is no reliable dose for achieving a cosmetic change, Arora said. Small studies have found visible changes after about six weeks of eating extra servings of fruits and vegetables, though results can vary. The color also fades gradually after a person cuts back, he noted.
Dermatologists warn that a carotenoid glow does not protect skin from UV exposure. (iStock)
That pigment buildup, known as carotenemia, is generally harmless, Arora said, but skin that turns yellow-orange without a dietary change should be evaluated by a health care professional.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
The food trick does avoid skin damage caused by UV exposure, which also raises the risk of skin cancer and premature aging.
"The carotenoid glow involves no UV damage at all, but it also gives you no meaningful sun protection," Arora warned. "'Carrot color' is not a substitute for sunscreen."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Dermatologists also caution that carotenoid supplements taken for a tan may carry risks for certain people. (iStock)

Arora cautioned against taking high-dose carotenoid supplements for appearance, though. High-dose beta-carotene supplements have been linked to increased lung cancer risk in people who smoke or used to smoke, according to the National Institutes of Health’s Office of Dietary Supplements.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
For people seeking a bronzed look, Arora recommends self-tanners, professional spray tans, bronzers or tinted sunscreen. He advises pairing them with broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every day.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Eating a colorful, carotenoid-rich diet is great for your overall health," he said. "I’d treat the glow as a bonus, not the goal."
Deirdre Bardolf is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital.

title: Iconic MTV star turns 60, shares her no-guilt approach to fitness, food and aging well
summary: Daisy Fuentes shares her 20-minute strength training routine, menopause sleep tips and the guilt-free "anti-hustle era" that keeps her strong at 60.
story: As Daisy Fuentes turns 60, the TV personality and lifestyle entrepreneur has traded superficial beauty pressures for a low-key wellness routine — built on 20-minute workouts, a "magical" sleep trick and a guilt-free "anti-hustle era."
During her 1990s rise as an MTV icon and supermodel, Daisy Fuentes admitted that "being cute" was her top priority.
Now, as she enters her 60s, the TV personality and lifestyle entrepreneur has traded superficial beauty pressures for a more grounded approach to health.

Speaking with Fox News Digital, Fuentes, who is primarily based in Los Angeles, opened up about embracing a guilt-free "anti-hustle era" — sharing her 20-minute workouts, a "magical" sleep trick and the surprisingly simple habits that keep her rested and strong.
JENNIFER ANISTON’S SECRET TO STAYING FIT AT 57 STARTS WITH ONE SIMPLE WORKOUT ROUTINE
Fuentes’ health and wellness priorities have shifted a great deal in the decades since she started modeling and appearing on TV in her late teens and 20s, she shared.

"In that era, I was more focused on, how can I look better? How can I lose a few pounds to look better in certain clothes? It was very superficial. And as the years have passed, health and wellness has started to become an inside job," Fuentes said.
As Daisy Fuentes turns 60, the TV personality and lifestyle entrepreneur has traded superficial beauty pressures for a low-key wellness routine. (Daisy Fuentes Instagram/Celeste Canino)

"When you start realizing that most of your life has already happened, how you want to live your life now … becomes more about being present and being able to enjoy the time that you have left," she added.
LONGEVITY DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT MATTERS MOST FOR AGING WELL, BEYOND PRICEY BIOHACKS
Amid the litany of longevity-focused tips and tricks circulating online, Fuentes said she strives to keep it simple and not be "obsessive" about health and wellness.
"On social media, depending on your algorithm, you can get bombarded and overwhelmed with all the [things] that you're supposed to be doing and not doing," she said.
Model and TV personality Daisy Fuentes poses for portraits around September 1993. (Getty Images)

"Yes, some of those things are smart … I do a lot of the things, but I also realized at a certain point that it's much more important to have fun, to be present, to not obsess, and to leave a little room for the unexpected."
Optimizing sleep
As Fuentes entered her 50s, she started to experience some sleep challenges, which she attributed to fluctuating hormones during menopause.

"Balancing out my hormones [and] going on HRT [hormone replacement therapy] helped tremendously," she said. "It got me feeling back to my old self, where the minute I got in bed, I would do a little scrolling and all of a sudden my eyes would start closing."
10-MINUTE FITNESS HABIT CAN HELP ADULTS OVER 40 MAINTAIN MUSCLE AND STAY STRONG

Although Fuentes admits that she breaks a few traditional "sleep hygiene" rules — such as scrolling on her phone in bed – she does wear red-light-blocking glasses and strives to keep her social media algorithm strictly positive.
Fuentes said she relies on what she describes as a total "sensory experience" to stay asleep, including wearing a silk eye mask.
Fuentes said she strives to keep it simple and not be "obsessive" about health and wellness. (Celeste Canino)
"Right as I'm going to sleep, I pop that mask on, and it's almost like magic," she said. "It does something to your brain. It relaxes you." She also uses an air purifier that provides white noise.
"Our room is set up for sleep," Fuentes said. "We don't hear anything, we don't see anything and it is a sensory experience … a routine that instantly prepares your mind for what it needs to do."
Moving through life
When it comes to fitness, Fuentes said she strives for consistency, but, above all, listens to her body.

A key component of her routine is strength training, which she does four or five times a week. "That doesn't mean it has to be long … I can do a full-body weight training in 20 minutes, and that's what's important to me right now," she said.
WOMEN WHO START COMMON HORMONE THERAPY IN THEIR 50S MAY HAVE 23% LOWER DEMENTIA RISK
Other mainstays of Fuentes’ fitness regimen include Pilates, walking and staying active outdoors. "That's what keeps me and my mind really feeling better," she said.
A key component of Fuentes' fitness routine is strength training, which she does four or five times a week. (iStock)
"Sometimes I get on a vibration plate with my weights and just do 15 minutes of that, doing a plank, doing some sit-ups on it, some squats — I just try to do whatever I can," Fuentes said.
"Some days I have more energy, some days I don't, and I don't beat myself up about it. I do what I feel like doing and as long as I'm doing something, I'm OK."
Eating for longevity

When it comes to nutrition, Fuentes’ biggest shifts over the last decade were driven by physical changes during menopause. Noticing stubborn weight gain around her midsection in her mid-50s, she said she scaled back to about two meals a day and eliminated mindless snacking.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"I try to make it very protein-based," she said. "I start my day with a coffee that already has 20 grams of protein in it ... And if I'm having a snack in the middle of the afternoon, it's going to be protein-packed yogurt with some nuts and berries."
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

While Fuentes adopted a vegetarian, plant-based diet in her mid-40s, she emphasized that healthy eating doesn't require an "all-or-nothing" mindset, encouraging others to lean into more whole foods that match their lifestyle and preferences.
Embracing an ‘anti-hustle’ lifestyle
After decades of fast-paced working – both on and off-screen – Fuentes made a conscious decision in her late 40s to embrace a slower pace of life.
Fuentes shared her gratitude for being able to enjoy time with her husband, musician Richard Marx, whom she met in her mid-40s. (Getty Images)

"Ambition that never ends is something that I think needs to be adjusted as we flow through life," she said, adding that she no longer desires to "be out there and be chosen" the way she did in her 30s.

"I started embracing the fact that I am in this era of my life where I don't want to work like when I was 30 … and it's OK to feel proud of myself for what I have accomplished," she said. "I don't want to feel guilty for enjoying the fruits of my labor, for enjoying my life now."
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

When it comes to decompressing, Fuentes said she recharges by spending quiet time in the home spaces she loves decorating. Some of her favorite ways to unwind include reading, having tea with a friend, sitting in her backyard or taking an hour-long walk.
"I don't want to feel guilty for enjoying the fruits of my labor, for enjoying my life now."
Fuentes shared her gratitude for being able to enjoy time with her husband, musician Richard Marx, whom she met in her mid-40s.

"Finding love and finding your person later in life made me feel so grateful to have the time to spend with him," she said. "Why would I want to pretend to be busy doing something when what really fills my heart is to be with him, to have fun, to do what I want to do right now?"
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
While Fuentes acknowledged that she is in a "privileged" and fortunate position, she pointed out that she spent decades sacrificing to earn it.
Stepping into her "anti-hustle era" in her 50s and 60s, she said, is about questioning whether you are staying busy out of habit — or are ready to embrace a new, more fulfilling stage of life.
Melissa Rudy is senior health editor and a member of the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to melissa.rudy@fox.com.

title: Jennifer Aniston’s secret to staying fit at 57 starts with one simple workout routine
summary: Jennifer Aniston trains three to four times a week with PVOLVE, and a trainer says consistency, plus added weight training, are key to her fitness success.
story: Melanie Ramos, PVOLVE trainer, reveals that Jennifer Aniston trains three to four times a week, focusing on consistency and incorporating more weight training.
At 57 years old, Jennifer Aniston seems to be defying the laws of aging — but it doesn’t come without hard work.
The "Friends" actress has been public about practicing PVOLVE, a functional fitness method grounded in movement longevity.

The workouts prioritize mobility and stability through twisting and reaching motions that translate directly to everyday life. Combining sculpting, cardio and weight training, the method is designed to build muscle mass and support bone density.
10-MINUTE FITNESS HABIT CAN HELP ADULTS OVER 40 MAINTAIN MUSCLE AND STAY STRONG
According to PVOLVE trainer Melanie Ramos, what keeps Aniston looking and feeling her best isn't a specific workout buzzword, it's consistency.

"She's very consistent," Ramos told Fox News Digital. "She trains about three to four times a week doing PVOLVE, and she trains in all our modalities. … She specifically is adding a lot more weight training into her routine."
Jennifer Aniston is pictured with her trainer Dani Coleman, VP of Training at PVOLVE. (Instagram @dani_bcoleman)
As people age, especially women, muscle mass begins to decline, according to Ramos, who serves as lead trainer at PVOLVE Soho in New York City.
"So, I think for [Aniston], the consistency and just adding that extra weight training really helps her look amazing," she said.
WANT TO AGE BETTER? RESEARCHERS SAY 4-MINUTE ROUTINE MAY HELP PREVENT DANGEROUS FALLS
According to research published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology, only about 20% of women regularly engage in strength training, with many opting for aerobic exercise instead.
While walking offers major benefits for overall health, pairing cardio with simple resistance work can lead to significantly stronger heart and longevity outcomes.
Jennifer Aniston, pictured in 2025, has been adding a lot more weight training into her routine, a PVOLVE trainer shared. (Rodin Eckenroth/FilmMagic)

Rather than feeling pressured to commit to a full-hour workout to see results, Ramos advised simply getting started, adding, "Something that [Aniston] really prioritizes is even just getting 15 minutes of movement. "
Starting with "baby steps" — aiming for at least three workouts per week, even if they're short — will help you feel "like you can achieve the goals you want," the trainer said.
YOUR WALKING SPEED MAY HOLD A CLUE TO HOW LONG YOU’LL LIVE, STUDY SUGGESTS

"And then build more of that lifestyle habit where it feels that you need that movement every day," Ramos continued. "Movement is a part of life, and as we age, we have to look at how we're moving our body."
Exercises for mobility and stability can help aging adults maintain balance and independence, the trainer said. (iStock)
Prioritizing strength training and gradually increasing muscular load helps build lean mass and improve bone density, according to the trainer.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
As the body naturally stiffens with age, Ramos noted, targeted mobility and stability exercises become essential for maintaining balance and independence.
3 core pillars of Aniston’s routine
To show how simple it is to get started, Ramos demonstrated three signature moves from Aniston’s routine — targeting mobility, strength and stability, using just a pair of dumbbells.

Stand with the legs spread apart, feet turned out with a soft bend in the knees.
Take two dumbbells and hold them down at the thighs with palms flipped forward.
Bicep curl up to where the dumbbells meet the shoulders. Repeat this lift and lower the movement.
Bending the knees deeper with each curl will target more leg strength, while also toning the upper body and increasing arm strength.
Modification: Bring the legs closer together for a smaller and softer squat.

Dropping one dumbbell, stand in the same wide-leg position and hold the weight with two hands.
Bring the dumbbell over the right shoulder as if slinging a laundry bag.
"Wood chop" the weight down to the left thigh, stepping the back ankle in and parallel while twisting the core.
Bend the front knee for extra leg strength.
Modification: If twisting is hard on the back, hug the dumbbell closer to the chest instead of over the shoulder for smaller movement. Limit the bend in the supporting leg.

Standing in a high lunge, hold the dumbbell in one hand at the shoulder. Hold the other arm straight out to the side.
Bend the knees to lunge deeper, then straighten. While coming up from the lunge, press the dumbbell up to the ceiling.
Getting into a deeper lunge will activate the quad muscles, while the overhead shoulder press targets the upper body.
