‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Winner Shane Beatty on His Victory: ‘I Played It Flawlessly’

Below, Katie and Victor speak to TODAY.com in a joint interview about the finale and share details about fruit-gate that viewers didn’t see, including why it was so difficult for the other players to believe Victor. Plus, Katie reveals if she regrets making Shane a Traitor.
This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Katie: “I will say, with the way that things panned out, I think that Rob (Raush’s) mentality of keeping Maura (Higgins) super close, just because she was his strongest alliance, and he could kind of maybe flirt his way through…”
Victor: “Tell me more about that.”

Katie: “That was bingo! But oh gosh, there’s so many good ones. I mean, Cirie (Field’s) social strategy is absolutely admirable. I knew I’m not going to be the smartest one in here. I’m not going to have the most real life experiences to base different situations off of. But I’m incredible with people. I was like, if I can just make these people feel guilty for sending home a friend, if I can do that, great. I mean, we made it to the end, even though we lost…”
Victor: “I mean, I’ll give you your flowers. Kudos!”
Katie: “Thank you so much. I think that that was the only thing that helped.”
Victor: “You did the damn thing, Katie.”

Victor: “I am surprised. I think maybe watching it back, for you guys, it looked really obvious. Everybody’s like, ‘Oh, that’s the hardest murder in plain sight ever.’ I don’t think that’s true at all because I feel like people are attributing people not believing me to my social game. When I think it was so hard for anybody to actually believe that the murder in plain sight was something like tossing a fruit or tossing an apple to somebody. But I mean, it was pretty obvious for me. I saw it and I felt it. I was like, ‘Oh, Tomica’s offering fruit right now. Like, why? It’s 10 o’clock at night. We’re going to a funeral!’”
Katie: “But that’s another factor that did make it so difficult … we don’t eat apples. We don’t eat fruit.”
Victor: “They have pretzels. They have cookies. What do you mean you’re going to eat a Fuji apple at 10:45? No. That was so suspicious to me.”
Katie: “Right place. Right time.”

Katie: “OK, and thank you so much for giving me praises. It actually wasn’t. So I looked smarter unintentionally. I was going to try to help. It’s funny because when you’re playing, you really aren’t thinking, ‘Oh, how are people going to perceive me?’ At least I wasn’t. I wasn’t thinking, ‘How is this going to look?’ I was just trying to do everything. But in this one moment, I was thinking, ‘OK, this is what tests the Traitors. A murder in plain sight is really the biggest piece of evidence Faithfuls can pick off of to discover a Traitor.’ I wanted to do it because I wanted to prove that I could do something hard and get away with it. Then, I went to go give (Victor) an apple, and I walked in with pretzels. You can actually see me when I go with him and Abby Lee into the billiard room. I’m holding pretzels in my hand. I just was going to try to read the room and be like, ‘Oh, I’m going to go get more pretzels and grab an apple and throw it at him.’ As soon as I walked in, he was like, ‘Tomica just offered me an apple. There’s a murder in plain sight!’ I was like, ‘Thank you, Lord, for not letting me walk in with an apple right now.’”
Victor: “I would have actually started crying. I was like, ‘Oh, they’re all around me. What is happening?’”
Katie: “So I was going to try, but you know, loudy pants over here just started saying, ‘There’s a murder in plain sight!’”

Victor: “I genuinely thought it was like a 1 vs. 20. I was like, oh, NBC is doing this new spin where there’s 20 Traitors versus me, and let’s like ‘Truman Show’ make this kid go crazy. But that’s the game. It really messes with you.”

Katie: “With super fans, or people that are fans of the show and love it, you know a lot of them wanted to be Traitors. That was like the biggest thing. Everyone just couldn’t shake the fact that we knew for a fact you did not walk in there and go, ‘I want to be a Faithful.’ So it’s like everyone’s in awe. It’s like, well, everyone could do it, and everyone probably wants to. That’s really a hard place to be, and I think that’s why everyone’s so skeptical of each other because we know we’ve seen the show.”

Katie: “I don’t have any regrets. I think that — and again, this could really be like a sign of weakness for me too — but I don’t think that I had fully come to terms with the fact that I should recruit someone who then I immediately go in the next day and throw them in. I was like, that would be not only evil but risky if it backfires on me. So I mean, it wasn’t even a fact of like, ‘Oh, I don’t want to do that.’ But it was just I was so afraid of picking the wrong person. Honestly, (Victor) had enough heat on him to where if I could have gone in and immediately flipped it on him, been like, ‘Guys, we need to get Victor today,’ and I had enough pull, sure. That’d be great. But if I didn’t, and it flips back on me…”
Victor: “Baby girl, I would’ve UNO reversed you so hard.”

Katie: “Exactly. I knew I couldn’t control him, so he was never an option. Wyatt (Gillespie), I just didn’t trust. I don’t think he would have wanted to. Abbey  (Benjamin). I really did want either Abbey B or Kriste. But again, I was just scared. Shane just had this, funny enough, effect that I didn’t think that he would go against me. I knew he would really try to work with me, and I think he did. I just think it got to a point where he couldn’t do any more. It would have thrown away his own game. So it is what it is. But I also weighed into effect, like, ‘OK, who would I be OK losing to?’ Couldn’t do (Victor). But I did anyway. So I mean that sucks.’
Victor: “In what order? Who got out first? I think it was her.”
Katie: “You’re right.”

Katie: “I didn’t share that. I let Wyatt and Abbey do that. But that was really fun. I think that gave our finalists a lot of clarity. And it’s what’s helped us stay close — is that we were able to kind of go back and forth on like, ‘You’re a Traitor. Oh my gosh, and you’re a Faithful.”

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Finalists Wyatt and Abbey on the ‘Shocking’ and Tear-Filled Finale: ‘Out of Body Feeling’
summary: Wyatt Gillespie and Abbey Benjamin break down Shane Beatty’s shocking “The Traitors: New Blood” reveal and win in interview with TODAY.com.
story: “The Traitors: New Blood” season finale delivered an emotional moment more dramatic than a reaction from any “Survivor” castaway, “Big Brother” player or Bravo housewife who has played the game.

During the epic conclusion of the all-civilian version of the show, which aired Nov. 19, winner Shane Beatty devastated Faithfuls Wyatt Gillespie and Abbey Benjamin when he revealed he was a Traitor. Wyatt and Abbey chose to end the game with Shane, thinking that only Faithfuls remained. But as a Traitor, Shane was crowned the sole winner and walked away with the $246,300 prize pot.
After realizing they had lost the game, Wyatt covered his face in disbelief and Abbey doubled over and sobbed. But after seeing Shane’s guilt and hearing his heartfelt explanation, they forgave him.

Wyatt and Abbey break down Shane’s shocking reveal below, and share if his last-minute recruit to the turret made it easier to forgive him. Plus, they reveal which Traitor they say all the players suspected and hatched a plan to eliminate episodes in advance.
This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Wyatt: “Not only was the finale devastating, finding out I was a Faithful was devastating. For the months before the show, when you’re interviewing and going through the process, I’m a Traitor. I am not a Faithful. I’m like, ‘It would be crazy for them to not choose me as a Traitor.’ I wanted it so bad. I thought I made a great pitch to Alan. I thought it was written I was a Traitor.

“But when I’m picked as a Faithful, I think immediately to myself, ‘All right, I need to think on the fly here. What is the most indicative way to be a Faithful?’ And it’s to fully immerse yourself. To fully be as emotional as possible, to make as many connections as possible and to really take whatever emotions you have and double them. Because then people can see the fear in your eyes. If you have genuine fear and paranoia every day waking up at the Round Table, people can see it. I think the reason the people who were at the finale got to the finale was because they were genuinely themselves. I think the best strategy here is to really be yourself as a Faithful because you wake up grounded in truth. When people can see you speak your truth, it’s very easy to know that they’re a Faithful.”

Abbey: “No, it really is. We end up turning on Michael (Foote). I loved and trust Michael. I did believe he was a Traitor, but I did want to take him out at that point. But Clyde (Moser) and Ben (McDonnell) had brought him up at the Round Table, and at that point I did think he was a Traitor. So I was like, ‘OK, I do have to go with my other dolls’ Clyde and Ben.’ I think (Wyatt) spoke on it, it’s the fear. They just had that natural fear. But honestly, too, we just are so stripped away to nothing. We’re so immersed playing the game. It’s a lot harder than it looks when you’re watching back. I think I just trusted them anyway. I was like, they have my back, and I’ll have theirs until they do something to show me otherwise. It worked pretty good with us until it didn’t.”

Wyatt: “I think a lot of the times when I would speak at the Round Table, or I’d speak to people just in reality, I was talking about like, ‘Oh my God, who’s walking into the breakfast room not scared?’ Or not as excited. To me, you start to find out Katie’s a Traitor like Episode 9, Episode 10. Because there’s nothing. She’s stone cold. She’s ready to go. There was always a sense that she was pulling the strings behind the scenes. I think to everybody it was pretty obvious Katie was a Traitor.”

Abbey: “It’s so funny that where you sit at Round Table is so important. Where Katie sat, I never could see her at Round Table. (Wyatt) sat right across from her. So I think that’s important too because you’re getting to watch their facial expressions the entire Round Table. I really started to buy into Katie being a Traitor when Ben thought it was her and he got murdered, and then Clyde thought it was Katie and then he got murdered. So after that, I was pretty certain. But honestly, wanted to hold on to her until the final fire because of course we didn’t know there had been a recruitment. (I) wanted to hold on to her, so we wouldn’t end up having a recruitment that had already happened.”

Wyatt: “It was part of the game play to keep Katie in the game because we all knew she was a Traitor. You send home Faithfuls because you want to end the game with the people you want to end the game with. It was part of the game plan to send Jay (Vinnedge) home because we know that Katie’s a traitor. We’ll get her out at the fire. That’s how it went down.”

Wyatt: “So you got to put yourself in my shoes, right? There is no ultimatum. There’s no recruitment that happened. The only person that I really have in my mind there is Katie. So on top of us knowing that Kriste (Lewis) wasn’t going to be in there, knowing that Jay wasn’t going to be in there … what you guys don’t see is I asked about the shield probably 50 times. I was like, ‘There’s no way somebody walked out of there without the shield.’ Shane and Victor and I are on the car ride on the way home, and he’s still lying to my face, so I’m freaking out. To me, it’s you vote him away because now this trust was just breached. It’s not that I think he’s a Traitor. No, it’s not (that) at all. It’s a risk that I think I have to just end this game with the Faithfuls I 100% trust. But, like, obviously Shane (laughs)...”

Abbey: “So at that point, it had gotten so close to the end, I think we all were feeling it. Because I had done very well about not being nervous or fearful the whole game. You don’t want to get so close to the end and lose. I think we all had these heightened emotions of, ‘I can’t get this far and fumble it.’ So to me, that part wasn’t as suspicious because we did all have a change in our behavior. He had played such a great Faithful game because obviously he was a Faithful before. Clyde leaving me the breadcrumbs of the heavy footsteps, that was the only thing that pointed to Shane. As a Faithful, you have to do the best with the information that you have, and I just couldn’t red him and vote him out because maybe it could have been him with heavy footsteps.”

Wyatt: “While Shane’s nervous to the viewer, we walk into breakfast every day, and we’re like, ‘I’m still alive. What is going on? Why are we here?’ As a Faithful, you want to display your emotions as much as possible to really confirm what people want to think about you. Shane’s nervous the entire time, and then he’s just more nervous. There’s not like a huge change in demeanor or someone’s character. Shane was always nervous. I was always nervous. That was how Shane and I bonded. We were like dapping each other up every breakfast. Like, ‘Oh my God, this feels so good to see you. My boy is still here.’ We would just throw our hands up in the air.”

Wyatt: “I interpreted things a little bit differently than Abbey because in both of our minds there was no recruitment, there was no ultimatum. It was so late in the game it wasn’t even a possibility to us. While that might seem naive, it was literally 24 hours. In my head, I’m looking at Shane and I see him cry while I’m crying and his crying is a little bit different than our crying. We’re excited crying and Shane has this feeling of guilt. I’m like, ‘Oh, oh no.’ I start to feel it in that moment. Then he finally says that he’s a Traitor and everything stops for me. I ran through every possibility except an ultimatum. He couldn’t even speak, and so I see him struggling so much, and that’s my boy at the same time. I’m thinking, I’m not going to let my guy feel like this. The feeling of guilt is way worse than the feeling I’m feeling of losing. So in that moment, just empathy takes over, and you go help your boy out. That’s what I had to do.”

Abbey: “I think for me, it didn’t change anything, him being recruited or if he was a Traitor the whole time. Because it’s the game, right? It’s called ‘The Traitors.’ So no matter if he was a Traitor from day one or right at the end, it doesn’t matter. He did what he was supposed to do, and that’s the game. There were definitely no hard feelings, but it was very difficult to process. Of course, looking back, it does make you feel a little bit better. Like, OK, we didn’t miss it because he did play a Faithful game most of the game because he was Faithful. God love Wyatt, he was processing with questions. Me, I was more processing with tears.”

Wyatt: “So I pretty much went from bull blown crying to interrogation. ‘Okay, how?’ Then he gave me the answer, and then I was like, ‘That’s my dog. I just got to help him out right now. That’s my boy.’
We’re all family. It’s crazy. You don’t want to see your loved ones hurt.”

Abbey: I had nothing that I could offer, words wise. I couldn’t speak. It’s very shocking and out-of-body feeling. You almost just kind of dissociate from your body. But we all got very close. Honestly, as heartbreaking as it was to lose, I’m so incredibly grateful for him. I’m honestly leaving this whole experience with such a grateful heart, and what a special experience that we got to compete and do and be involved in.
Wyatt: It’s a privilege to be in the most emotional finale of all time.

title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Stars Rock Their Body at Backstreet Boys Sphere Show
summary: Everybody rocked their body at the Backstreet Boys concert at Sphere in Las Vegas following the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
story: Everybody rocked their body at the Backstreet Boys concert in Las Vegas following the Las Vegas Grand Prix, including “Ted Lasso” stars.

The group hosted the official post-race show of the motor-sport competition at Sphere at The Venetian on Nov. 21, where they delivered a high-energy performance of their classic hits for fans and celebs.

Hannah Waddingham and Brendan Hunt were spotted dancing like no one was watching to “I Want It That Way.” Clapping their hands and lifting their arms, the duo were all smiles as Waddington made a heart shape with her hands.
Other notable stars who attended the concert included former Bachelorette Jenn Tran, who shared on her Instagram story she was “screaming, crying, throwing up” from excitement.

Before they took the stage, however, Howie Dorough, AJ McLean, Nick Carter, Brian Littrell and Kevin Richardson attended the Nov. 21 race, where stars like Terry Crews, Chris Pratt and more cheered on the teams.
They also had some fun checking out the BWT Alpine and the Mercedes-AMG Petronas garage, where they had members of the F1 teams sing their best rendition of “I Want It That Way.”
The five singers then gave them a hand by concluding the famous lyrics.

And then it was to Sphere where they showed up and showed out opening with “Larger Than Life” and singing “It’s Gotta Be You,” “As Long As You Love Me,” and more before closing out with “Everybody (Backstreet’s Back).”

The Backstreet Boys will return to the iconic venue for a series of December and January shows. They first announced their “Into the Millennium” Sphere residency on TODAY in February 2025 as a celebration of their 25th anniversary of their hit album “Millennium.”
At the time, the group expressed their continued gratitude for being able to share their music with their fans over the last three decades.

“We’ve been at this for 32 years, but to get to a point where we’re like the Rolling Stones of the pop world — they’ve been together for 60 years — we’re going to keep doing this until we probably physically can’t,” McLean told TODAY.com. “We truly love what we do.”

title: They Just Won the 2026 F1 Academy Championships. Alisha Palmowski, Rafaela Ferreira Talk Their Defining Season
summary: F1 Academy stars Alisha Palmowski, who won the 2026 Drivers’ Championship, and Rafaela Ferreira reflect on winning the 2026 Team title for Campos Racing.
story: Alisha Palmowski and Rafaela Ferreira have learned how to stay calm under pressure, helping Campos Racing win the 2026 F1 Teams’ Championship.

The Red Bull Academy Programme drivers reflect on their successful second year in the all-female Formula 4–level racing series and tell TODAY.com their improved confidence and execution over the last year secured them the top honors.

“Being at both of our second years, I think we were both able to take a lot of learnings from last year and just execute it a little bit better,” 20-year-old Palmowski, who clinched the 2026 Drivers’ title, says. “I was much more confident going into this year, a lot calmer. Just knew more of what to expect of the whole procedure of F1 Academy. A completely different driver and person than the driver who turned up to Shanghai last year.”
Ferreira, 21, who came in 11th overall in the individual competition, described the season as “a little bit more challenging,” yet is “very happy” with how the year went.

In its fourth year, the F1 Academy’s 2026 season consisted of 14 races across six rounds. It kicked off in March in Shanghai and ended Nov. 21 in Las Vegas, coinciding with the Formula 1 Grand Prix. The Susie Wolff-led initiative is on a mission to help young women get involved in motorsport.
Below, Campos Racing’s Palmowski and Ferreira share their early racing memories, what they wish people knew about F1 Academy and more.

Alisha Palmowski: I’ve always been the biggest F1 fan ever since I was a really young child. For as long as I can remember, I always grew up with the influence of it on TV. The first time I experienced F1 cars in real life would have been Silverstone in 2015 at the British Grand Prix. I think I was about 8 or 9 years old at the time, and I think that’s where my passion for motorsport was really unlocked. The speed, the sound, the smell, everything. I just got hooked instantly.

Rafaela Ferreira: I remember my dad showing me some races from (Brazilian driver) Ayrton Senna. I think it was when I started to watch F1. I think the first time I went to a Grand Prix was four years ago ... I was racing in a support series and I went to the track as well. So I was racing at the same time I was watching F1 for the first time. I think I was more worried about watching F1 than racing my race.

AP: I think how tough this series is. I think it’s often underestimated. In F1 Academy, we’re obviously an F4 level series, but I think we have different challenges to what other F4 level series have. Racing as a support series to F1, the amount of track evolution that we have across a race weekend. When F1 go out, lay their rubber down, the adaptability that we need from session to session, it’s very high. I think that’s where it really differs from a standard F4 level series. But if you progress through the ranks up to F2 or F3, they experience the exact same thing. So it’s giving us a great foundation to learn those basics and to take forward. That’s probably what people don’t realize is, it’s tough, it’s very difficult.

RF: I think it’s how much we work behind the scenes. It seems as if it’s just like seven rounds, but in the end we have a lot of things to do. We have a lot of work on the (simulators). When I was racing before in F4, we didn’t have a lot of work on the sim. We would just go to the track, do a lot of laps on the training, and then you’re gonna see how it’s gonna be. But here we have a lot of work on the sim, something that we need to learn as well. It’s very important.

RF: Canada this year was a very good race. I led the race from the start from the pole. The weekend was very competitive for me. I love Canada. I love to race on that track, so it was a very good weekend.

AP: Austin, to be honest. Actually wrapping up the championship. It’s what we worked towards all year. And it was a very high-pressure weekend because although I had the buffer to second place, it was like the elephant in the room. I know everybody expected it and wanted it to happen, but nobody really wanted to say it. So I tried to approach it very much as a normal race weekend, but it was very obvious that it wasn’t a normal race weekend. When I got in the car, there were like 30 photographers around my car. So, just the fact that I was able to stay calm under that pressure, I think that was what I was most proud of this year.

title: James Blunt’s Bizarre Name Change Gets a Royal Seal of Approval From Queen Camilla
summary: James Blunt promised to become Ryan Air if his album hit No. 1. It did, he filed the paperwork and Queen Camilla is already calling him Ryan.
story: For years, James Blunt has been the main target of his own jokes. Now Queen Camilla has joined in.
On Nov. 20, after the Royal Variety Performance at the Royal Albert Hall, Blunt was among the performers who met King Charles and the queen.
“Hello, Ryan — formerly known as James,” the queen said, according to British news reports and video shared on social media.

She was referring to a promise that started as a publicity stunt and seems to have ended at the deed poll office. Before his new album, “Airplane Mode,” came out, Blunt, 52, said that if it reached No. 1 on the British charts, he would legally change his name to Ryan Air, after the Irish budget airline.
His pitch: stream it, buy it, get it to No. 1, “otherwise, I’ll have to carry on being James Blunt... and nobody wants that.”
The fans listened, with help from one in particular.
“It’s number one!” Blunt told the PA news agency after the show. “My mother’s bought a lot of copies.”
It’s his first No. 1 album in Britain since “All the Lost Souls” in 2007. His 2005 debut, “Back to Bedlam,” spent 10 weeks at the top.

After first hinting in a video that he might back out, Blunt posted on Instagram an application to change his name from James Hillier Blount, his birth name, to Ryan Bel Air. “This cost me £53.05,” he wrote in the caption. (That’s about $70.)
The airline answered in his comments: “Our lawyers will be in touch.”
His wife, Sofia Wellesley, isn’t laughing. When PA asked whether he had really become Ryan Bel Air, Blunt winced.
“My wife is not pleased with me,” he said, adding that she might “change her name back to her maiden name.”

This is not the first time Blunt has put his name up as a bet. In 2024, he said he would let fans choose a new name for him if the 20th anniversary reissue of his debut album, “Back to Bedlam,” reached No. 1. The fans’ favorite was Blunty McBluntface. The album fell short, and he stayed James.
His stage name was already a change. Blunt has said he dropped the “o” from Blount because other children teased that it rhymed with an obscene word.
At the Royal Variety show, where he sang his new song “Circles,” the host Jason Manford introduced him as both James Blunt and Ryan Air.

title: Christopher Briney Shocks Jenna and Sheinelle With a Magic Trick on TODAY: ‘What?!’
summary: Christopher Briney proved his talents go beyond acting when he dazzled Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones with his magic skills on TODAY.
story: Christopher Briney proved his talents go beyond acting when he dazzled Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones with his magic skills on TODAY.
Briney demonstrated a two-card version of a magic trick called three-card monte, which he described as “a scam street game.”

In the trick, Jenna held a diamond card and Briney held a heart. He explained that the goal of the trick is to swap the two cards without her noticing. Briney then openly switched the cards to reveal that he now had diamonds and Jenna had hearts.
“Hold it tight. Don’t let me do that again,” he told Jenna.
“When they do it on the street, they do it real quick,” he added, as he demonstrated the sneaky move.
It seemed like Briney hasn’t swapped the cards at all and was instead just explaining how it all works behind the scenes.
Then came the real trick. He asked Jenna to flip over the two cards she had been holding — only now they were in the suits of spades and clubs.
“What?!” Jenna said. “Wait y’all, I never let go. I was holding really tight.”
The move left both Jenna and Sheinelle stunned.
“I think you’re really a magician,” Jenna said.
“Not gonna lie, my mind’s kind of blown,” Sheinelle added.
The actor appeared on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle to discuss his latest project, the Christmas rom-com, “Clashing Through the Snow,” which lands on Prime Video on Nov. 23.

His character, Ryan is a book editor who finds himself having to travel across the country with a rival editor, Hannah, played by Michelle Randolph, as both race to lock down career-saving book deals.
Jenna pointed out that this character is a more “comedic role” for Briney, who said that’s what drew him to the film.

But playing a romantic lead is nothing new for Briney. The actor is best known for his role as pensive heartthrob Conrad Fisher in “The Summer I Turned Pretty” series, the TV adaptation of the book trilogy by Jenny Han.
“The Summer I Turned Pretty” will continue with a movie, set after the events of 2025’s Season 3. Briney confirmed the movie has already filmed.
Briney said making the film, which does not yet have a release date, was “great,” adding, “the people on that show mean a lot to me.”

title: How Do Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson Appear in ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’?
summary: What happens in the “Sunrise on the Reaping” epilogue scene with Jennifer Lawrence’s Katniss, Josh Hutcherson’s Peeta and Woody Harrelson’s Haymitch.
story: Warning: Spoilers ahead for the ending to “Sunrise on the Reaping.”
“Sunrise on the Reaping” is set more than 20 years before the events of the first “Hunger Games” film, but it still features an appearance from Katniss Everdeen — twice.
Based on Suzanne Collins’ 2025 novel of the same name, “Sunrise on the Reaping,” which hit theaters Nov. 20, is the second “Hunger Games” prequel story.
Where “Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes” told the origin story of President Snow, “Sunrise on the Reaping” follows Haymitch Abernathy.

In 2012’s “The Hunger Games,” Haymitch, played by Woody Harrelson, is introduced as the oft-intoxicated, perpetually cynical District 12 Games victor serving as Katniss and Peeta’s mentor. He’s largely unlikable but honest, and steps up to support his tributes in the arena when he can.

By the end of the trilogy with “Mockingjay,” it’s revealed Haymitch has deep-seated alliances with other victors of the Games, and he becomes one of the reluctant leaders of the revolt against the Capitol.
Before “Sunrise on the Reaping,” fans only knew the basics of his story: He won the 50th Hunger Games, aka the Second Quarter, which had twice as many tributes.

The novel and film, starring Joseph Zada as 16-year-old Haymitch, go deep into how that went down, from his unconventional reaping, how he become a rebel, the roots of his alcoholism and finally, why he lives all alone in Victor’s Village.
But on the Oct. 28 episode of “Call Her Daddy,” Jennifer Lawrence confirmed she and Josh Hutcherson, who starred as Peeta, will appear in the new film. Here’s how.
Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson Pop up At the Very End of the Film

“Sunrise on the Reaping” is much darker compared to previous franchise installments. Essentially every person Haymitch loves or grows to love throughout the film is dead by the end. And even the people who haven’t been killed by Snow and the Capitol, Haymitch’s fear of making them a target leads him to push them away.

This includes his friend from District 12 Burdock and his eventual wife, Asterid. When Haymitch returns after winning the Hunger Games, he’s iced out by most of the district due to the Capitol’s portrayal of Haymitch as ruthless, selfish and cowardly. But Burdock still tries to connect with his old friend, especially in the wake of the deaths of his family and girlfriend, Lenore Dove, in sudden tragedies.

Haymitch turns to alcohol and withdraws from society, living in Victor’s Village. As time passes, he’s forced year after year to mentor the next set of tributes in the Games as District 12’s only winner.

One of the final scenes sees Haymitch in the woods. He sees Burdock and Asterid out in nature with a newborn. He hides behind a tree as he watches the scene with the happy family. He locks eyes with the baby as she’s carried over her dad’s shoulder. He also overhears the parents coo their baby girl’s name: Katniss.
Yes — Haymitch’s old friends are Burdock and Asterid Everdeen, Katniss Everdeen’s parents.
That’s only the first time the character pops up.
“Sunrise on the Reaping” has an epilogue, set well after the events of “Mockingjay” and the end of the annual Hunger Games.

In the scene, Woody Harrelson reprises his role as Haymitch and stands in District 12 before a memorial dedicated to those killed by the Capitol. Lawrence’s Katniss and Hutcherson’s Peeta join him. They have a conversation reflecting on the end of the war and their newfound peace and wish Haymitch a happy birthday. It brings the film’s beginning, which reveals Haymitch’s birthday always fell on reaping day, full circle.

The somber moment also shows that Haymitch was eventually able to make Lenore Dove’s wish — “don’t let the sun rise on the reaping” — come true, as Haymitch was part of the forces that ended the Hunger Games for good.
Viewers later see Haymitch sitting in the field he used to meet Lenore Dove in. He’s surrounded by geese, an animal Lenore Dove used to raise.
What Have the ‘Hunger Games’ Star Said About Their Cameo?
After Lawrence shared that she appears in “Sunrise on the Reaping,” she called her experience returning to the franchise “unbelievable.”
“It was so crazy, because it was the same crew,” she said. “Josh and Woody — it was so emotional. Josh and I like, didn’t walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other.”
“And Woody obviously came through the window of my hotel room uninvited,” she added with a grin. “It wouldn’t be the same if he listened to boundaries and used a door.”

Lawrence, Hutcherson and Harrelson also attended the premiere of “Sunrise on the Reaping” in New York on Nov. 16 and appeared together in the cold open for “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon” that same night.

title: Gwyneth Paltrow Explains Her Viral Dairy-Arugula Substitution — But We’re Still a Little Confused
summary: Gwyneth Paltrow says she “didn’t mean to break the internet” with her arugula tip and reveals her Thanksgiving menu, canned cranberry and all.
story: Six months after a handful of chopped greens sent the internet into a tailspin, Gwyneth Paltrow is ready to clear the air.

When the Oscar winner returned to TODAY on Nov. 23 to talk about her new weekly video series, “The Goop Guide with Gwyneth Paltrow,” now streaming on Netflix and Spotify, it didn’t take long for Savannah Guthrie to bring up the elephant — or rather, the salad — in the room.
“I thought you were gonna mention the last time you were here,” Savannah told her. “Remember … our viral arugula.”
Back in May, Paltrow stopped by Studio 1A to make turkey meatballs. Mid-recipe, she offered a tip for anyone skipping dairy: dice up some arugula and toss it in.

Savannah’s perplexed on-air reaction quickly became the consensus online. Commenters joked about stirring leafy greens into their coffee and pancake batter, Food Network star Sunny Anderson filmed herself sipping a cup topped with arugula, and Goop itself got in on the fun with a photo of a cookie perched on a cup of greens.
After TODAY replayed the now-infamous clip, Paltrow explained what she was going for.
“What I meant to say is, if you chop up arugula and put it in a meatball, you don’t have to put the cheese in,” she said. “It’s like a substitute for Parmesan.”
Savannah wasn’t totally sold. “But it doesn’t taste like cheese,” she pointed out.
“It doesn’t,” Paltrow agreed. “But it gives it like this, you know, umami-ish like punch. So it’s a great flavor substitute. But I didn’t mean to break the internet.”
“I know, like the internet collapsed,” Savannah said.
As for a follow-up act? Paltrow is stumped. “Now I feel like, what are we gonna do for an encore?” she said.
Savannah also borrowed a question Paltrow likes to ask guests on her podcast: “What is the goopiest thing about you?” Savannah joked that her own answer is being friends with Paltrow.

Paltrow’s answer was a bit more introspective. “I think the goopiest thing about me is that I have insatiable curiosity, and to me, goop represents curiosity,” she said. “You know, like going into new areas.”
When it comes to Thanksgiving, though, Paltrow isn’t looking to try anything new. Don’t expect a gluten-free, dairy free spread at her house this week.
“Well, it’s not very goopy because there’s a lot of dairy and gluten and sugar,” she said.
The menu includes her grandmother’s “famous stuffing” and Martha Stewart’s roast turkey recipe. “I’ve tried a lot, and that’s I think the best,” she explained.
The whole crew will be at the table, too. “Everybody’s coming home,” Paltrow said. “Got all four kids, my husband, and family and friends. It’s going to be fun.”
And yes, there will be cranberry sauce — straight from the can.
“I read that you’re a canned cranberry girly,” Savannah said.
“I am,” Paltrow admitted. “That is not very goopy of me.”
Her pick is Ocean Spray jellied cranberry sauce, can ridges and all. “There’s no replacement,” she said. “Delicious.”
Before the segment wrapped, Savannah squeezed in one last callback, offering her guest a little green “creamer” for her coffee.
“Cheers,” Savannah said.

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Winner Shane Beatty on His Victory: ‘I Played It Flawlessly’
summary: Shane Beatty opens up about his emotional win and end game strategy, and responds to those criticizing his victory in an interview with TODAY.com.
story: Shane Beatty has joined a small group of players who have won “The Traitors,” and he knows he earned his spot in the winner’s circle.

The New York native was crowned the winner of “The Traitors: New Blood,” the first all-civilian version of the show, during the tear-filled season finale on Nov. 19. For most of the game, Shane played as a Faithful, and all the players trusted him. But after two Traitors were banished, remaining Traitor Katie Fites gave Shane an ultimatum: join her in the turret or die.
He accepted her offer and became a Traitor for the last few episodes of the season. He continued to present as a Faithful and successfully deceived the other players, winning the $246,300 prize pot.
“I did every aspect of this game, and I played it flawlessly,” he tells TODAY.com.

But his victory was emotional, as Shane had to deliver the stunning news to allies Wyatt Gillespie and Abbey Benjamin that he was Traitor. All three wept after the reveal before embracing and celebrating Shane’s victory.

Shane unpacks that heartbreaking and heartwarming moment and explains how he navigated the end of the game below. He also shares why he always knew Katie wouldn’t win and how he feels about critics who discredit his victory.
This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

“It feels like the weight is off my shoulders. I did it. I played every aspect of this game. The superpower, Faithful, Traitor, winning the game, having to betray my alliance, having to backstab somebody. I did every aspect of this game, and I played it flawlessly. Name was never written down at the Round Table! The Traitor hunter, he was in my back pocket. Listen, Victor (Vollbrechthausen) was in my pocket ever since I pardoned him, and he never suspected me.
I did it all, and it feels amazing.”

“So with Victor, it was at the pardon. It’s not even that I had an alliance with him yet. It was like, ‘Yes, I voted for you, but your demeanor isn’t giving off that I’m caught. I’m a Traitor.” So I’m like, all right, let’s pardon this dude. It’s not him. He looked like he wanted to throw it in my face, all of our faces, and be like, ‘You’re wrong. I’m a Faithful.’ So me and Victor’s alliance started once he voted out the first Traitor. I was like, ‘Whoa, fruit-gate is real! This is a thing. I’m sticking with this guy.’

“Wyatt was always my dog. Because you see how nervous I am on camera. I look crazy! I’m at breakfast stressing out. But me and Wyatt were always stressing. Every day, we’re talking about, ‘Oh my gosh! I hope I’m making another day. This is crazy. We’re losing bad. Faithfuls are down bad.’ So we were always bonding with that. Outside of the castle, he went to Syracuse University. My fiancé went to Syracuse University. I spent a lot of time in Syracuse. My fiancée’s parents are Syracuse alumni. His type of work has to do with my line of work, and we’re both in New York City. Automatically, we’re kicking it. We were trusting each other. But the boys’ alliance, us three, didn’t start until after we got out Tomica.”
“We, the boys, thought it was Kriste (Lewis), Katie or even both of them. So I was so shocked seeing that it was Katie and it’s not both of them. I’m thinking also, ‘We got this.’”

“We knew it was Katie, but we thought it was Kriste and Katie. So we were going to string Katie along and get out Kriste first. But we were going to get Kriste at the last Round Table and then Katie at the Fire of Truth, because we thought if we get out Kriste the time we got out Jay (Vinnedge), that they would recruit somebody again. But they recruited me already. Even if we got out Kriste, they were never going to recruit anybody else because I was recruited. We were always going to get out Katie, which made my situation very difficult because she wants me to try to convince the boys. But the boys already know it’s you, Katie! So there’s no convincing Victor and Wyatt and Abbey. There’s nothing I could try.
“I’m not sticking my neck out on the line just to burn myself. Would never happen. And I told her, ‘There’s heat on you.’”

“It’s not even that my loyalty really switched. I gave her something to work with. I’m like, ‘Listen, don’t even waste it on Victor. If you want to get out Victor, he has the shield.’ If I was truly still loyal to them, I wouldn’t have mentioned nothing about the shield. I could have had her try to attempt to go for Victor and then try to use that information. I was kind of loyal to her. She was already going to get voted out at the final fire. Abbey. Wyatt. Victor. That’s three votes. Even if I didn’t vote for her, she was always going to leave.”

“Nope, never. I was like, ‘Listen, if Ben thinks it’s you, we are going to go for Ben. Who else are we going to go for? Not one of my boys. I need them for votes.’ She wanted to do Ben. So if you want to do Ben, you’re steering it.

“Clyde mentioned my name. So if he mentioned my name, I definitely want to get him out of here. We don’t need a situation where they never murdered Victor, and then Clyde keeps going on about it, I’m at the final fire, and now I’m gone because we didn’t get rid of Clyde earlier.”

“That moment was one of the hardest things I had to face. Looking at somebody, knowing that I’m the reason they’re crying like this — I hate watching people cry. I hate making people cry. It doesn’t make me feel good. But I had to do it. It was so hard to do. I felt so guilty. I’m like, ‘This is my fault. I’m the reason why they’re crying.’ But the game is the game. What am I going to do? I have to do it.

“What am I going to say? ‘I’m a Traitor. I just forfeit, guys, because I feel bad that I have to tell you that I’m a Traitor.’ No, I’m going to follow through. It killed me. It hurt me. But they came to comfort me. Plot twist. They were like, ‘You know what? I understand why you did this, and we can see that the guilt is weighing heavy on you, G. Good game, and come give me a hug. Listen, we forgive you. It’s no hard feelings. The game is the game. If they were me, they would have done the same thing.’”

“That moment was such a blur. I wasn’t counting the time. I just remember crying and just not even being able to look at them, and then Wyatt (and Abbey), just coming up and surrounding me with their arms and just hugging me.”

“Haters are gonna hate. Listen, Jalen Brunson might have most of the points, but OG Anunoby still has to tip in that ball for them to win. He didn’t have as many points as everybody else. Somebody still got to knock it out the park, and I knocked it out the park. I gave everybody a great ending, and ultimately they’re saying, ‘Oh, easy win.’ No! You know how hard it is to build up that type of trust? As great as the game Victor played, he still didn’t have the trust at the end for them to get rid of him. I had to save Victor. I had to become a Traitor and do what I had to do.

“It doesn’t matter. Listen, I got the w. Alan Cumming said it himself. I’m number seven greatest of all time to play this game. Alan stamped it. What do you have to say about Alan calling me one of the greatest of all times? That’s what I have to say to them.

“The wedding planning is not in motion. Nothing has happened really yet because I didn’t have the money to book a venue, didn’t have the money to get the wedding planning started. But I have a guest list, and I’ve (expanded) my guest list to my cast. That’s where we’re at with it.”

title: See Jane Fonda on the Cover of Relaunched Life Magazine, Re-Creating a Moment from 1968
summary: Jane Fonda graces the cover of the newly relaunched Life, holding the 1968 copy of the magazine that she first appeared on solo.
story: Jane Fonda graces the cover of the newly relaunched Life, holding the 1968 copy of the magazine that she first appeared on solo.

The two-time Oscar winner, who turns 89 on Dec. 21, is one of Life Magazine’s six cover stars for the relaunch of the quarterly publication. Life returned with a new issue on Nov. 23, exactly 90 years after its first issue debuted. Life Magazine originally ending publication of the magazine in 2000.

TODAY has an exclusive first look at Fonda’s cover of the premiere issue, titled “Where Are We Now?” In the photo, she covers part of her face with the March 20, 1968, edition of the magazine, which featured her in costume for the cult classic sci-fi movie “Barbarella,” directed by her then-husband Roger Vadim.

The former “Grace and Frankie” star first appeared on the original magazine’s cover alongside her famous father, Hollywood legend Henry Fonda, in February 1960. She was 22. She would go on to pose for the magazine multiple times, including her first solo cover for Life in 1968, during her equally luminous acting career.
In an accompanying interview, Fonda, a longtime political activist, told the magazine she’s as optimistic as ever.
“I say hope is a muscle. When you use it, it flourishes,” Fonda said.

Other celebrities featured on the new Life’s cover include Olympic gold medalist Alysa Liu, online influencer iShowSpeed, actor John Malkovich, Neuralink brain implant recipient Noland Arbaugh and Andrew Jarrell, an Alaskan commercial fisherman whose photographs document life on the Bering Sea.
The original Life Magazine was launched as a weekly publication in 1936.

The relaunch “honors those founding principles” while reimagining “how they come to life in the modern era, delivering thoughtful, visually driven narratives that explore the human experience, individual ambition, and the cultural shifts shaping our world today,” the publication said in a press release.
The quarterly print magazine will also act as a “physical anchor” to a digital platform at new.life.com, which features original reporting, photography, documentary films and video content.
The relaunch is backed by Bedford Media company, which is owned and financed by supermodel and entrepreneur Karlie Kloss and her husband, Joshua Kushner.

title: Jennifer Garner Shares How She Struggled With Fame After the Success of ‘Alias’
summary: Jennifer Garner has long been a household name, gracing our screens for years in a number of iconic roles.
story: Jennifer Garner has long been a household name, gracing our screens for years in a number of iconic roles.

But the West Virginia native was once a chemistry student at Denison University in Ohio, who decided to switch her major to theater — a move that paid off. In 2001, she landed her breakout role as agent Sydney Bristow in ABC’s “Alias.”
“I stood in one place in my kitchen, reading the pilot, and never moved,” Garner said of her first impression of the script. “It was — it still is — the most arresting thing I have ever read.”

The actor, 54, sat down with TODAY’s Willie Geist on Sunday Sitdown to reflect on her career. Garner said that “Alias” changed “everything,” skyrocketing her to fame and placing her in the spotlight in a way that was difficult to process.
“I had a lot of missteps,” Garner told Willie. “I don’t care what you say or, you know, how grounded you are, it really messes things up for a couple of years.”
Garner said that at the time, she felt “embarrassed.”

“I was like that character in ‘The Peanuts’ who always has the dust cloud around him,” Garner said, referring to the lovably dusty Pigpen. “I was like that, but with paparazzi. And so it was just so uncomfortable. You just can’t connect with people, anymore.”

Garner, who spent five seasons on “Alias” went on to dazzle in renowned films, “13 Going on 30,” “Juno” and “Dallas Buyer’s Club,” in addition to television shows like Peacock’s “Five Star Weekend,” released in July.

Garner, who’s also the co-founder and chief brand officer of organic children’s snack food company Once Upon a Farm, told Willie that many of her latest projects have been mainly filmed in her home of Los Angeles which, as a mom of three, is a major plus.
“We all get to go home and see our kids, put them to bed,” she said. Garner added, however, that her kids “stay up way later than I do, every night.”
Garner shares three children with ex-husband Ben Affleck, to whom she was married for over a decade.
“Ben has been a very flexible — and great — co-parent,” Garner said of Affleck.
Both Garner and Affleck have been open about their co-parenting relationship. Earlier this year, Affleck also sat down with Willie and praised his ex-wife, calling her a “spectacular” mom.
“There’s no one-upping her, you know what I mean, on the parent thing,” Affleck said, joking.
Affleck added that “she’s not somebody that I would wanna get into a parenting competition with.”

“I respect her. I’m grateful for her,” Affleck said. “We got a really good thing where, it’s the only other person in the world who cares as much about the things I care the most about as I do, you know?”

title: ‘DWTS’ Pro Says Fans Are Using Votes To ‘Manipulate the Show’ After Latest Shocking Elimination
summary: The latest elimination on hit reality competition show “Dancing With The Stars” has drawn massive backlash — including from one of its own pros. Sharna Burgess, a pro who was paired with former contestant and reality personality Tyler Cameron on this season, expressed her disappointment in the show’s controversial voting system in a Nov. 20 Instagram story.
story: The latest elimination on hit reality competition show “Dancing With The Stars” has drawn massive backlash  — including from one of its own pros.

Sharna Burgess, a pro who was paired with former contestant and reality personality Tyler Cameron on this season, expressed her disappointment in the show’s controversial voting system in a Nov. 20 Instagram story. “DWTS,” as viewers know, uses a combination of judges scores and fan votes to determine which contestants move on to the next week.

In her Instagram story, Burgess had responded to a fan question about the recent exit of actor Harry Shum Jr. and his partner Jenna Johnson, a pair who had been seen as among the strongest contenders of the season, even receiving perfect scores on their two routines during their final night on the show.
In her post, seen by TODAY.com, Burgess wrote that she was “sadly” not surprised by the exit.

“I felt it was going to be another shock elimination. Not because they deserved it but simply because the online discourse is so wild that it’s was pretty clear who fans were ‘voting off’ and how they have felt about dance experience contestants,” said Burgess, referencing the way in which viewers have been critical of the competition’s inclusion of celebrities like Shum, who have a background in dance.

Burgess went on to say that viewers have been using their votes to “manipulate the show,” writing that it’s “so disappointing to see our voting system is now being used by viewers to vote people off instead of voting for your favorite.”
“This voting ppl off thing is so insanely negative and not what we are built on and it’s seemingly given fans the chance to manipulate the show,” she wrote.

Representatives from “Dancing with The Stars” did not respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment on Burgess’ Instagram story. Nor did they respond to requests for information on the show’s use of votes and how eliminations are determined.

As it stands, contestants are ranked on a “leaderboard” based on judges’ scores. Viewers can influence who remains on the show by voting for their preferred couple online or by text, according to ABC. Fans are permitted to submit 10 votes per couple, per voting method, which comes out to a total of 20 votes per couple.

While viewers are encouraged to vote for their “favorite,” critics have accused some fans of using their votes to protest certain contestants instead. Those with a history in dance in particular, like Shum and fellow recently-eliminated celeb Jenna Dewan, have been targeted with online harassment as some fans argue that they have an unfair advantage on a show that features celebrities of non-dance backgrounds.
In Burgess’ eyes, fans should be given a cap on votes.
“I say we got back to yall only have 10 votes total and you have to figure out how to dish them out,” she wrote in her Instagram story.

Given the controversies around the voting system, fans have long called for more transparency into how fan votes are weighted against judges’ scores. “DWTS” did not respond to TODAY.com’s request for an explanation, showrunner Conrad Green told the Hollywood Reporter last year that “it’s 50/50, effectively.”

“When you see the judges’ leaderboards, say there’s five couples and you’re in first place on that leaderboard, you get five judges ranking points. If you’re in second place, you get four, if you’re in third place, you get three, [fourth place,] two, [and fifth place,] one,” he told the outlet. “We do the same with the amount of public votes. You add those two [separate] ranking points together, and the couple with the lowest combined total of those ranking points goes home.
If there’s a tie, Green explained, the couple with the fewest public votes is eliminated.

The latest elimination marks the second week in which a dancer has gone home. Dewan exited the show during its Grammy Night episode Nov. 10. She, like Shum, also endured online harassment for her background as a dancer.

title: Prince Harry Had a Sweet Reaction to Robert Pattinson Being Cast As James Bond
summary: During a Nov. 20 appearance on UK show “This Morning,” Prince Harry was asked about Robert Pattinson’s casting as British secret agent James Bond in the upcoming 007 film. And it sounds like Pattinson’s got the Duke of Sussex on his side.
story: The prince has spoken!

During a Nov. 20 appearance on UK show “This Morning,” Prince Harry was asked about Robert Pattinson’s casting as British secret agent James Bond in the upcoming 007 film. And it sounds like Pattinson’s got the Duke of Sussex on his side.
“I can’t wait to see it,” he said.

Pattinson’s casting was announced earlier this week. He is set to step into the role for a Bond film that will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, the brains behind the “Dune” trilogy. He will be the seventh person to take on the iconic role, with his predecessor being Daniel Craig.

During his appearance on the show, Harry took part in a game in which he had to choose between British and American options. When asked to pick between the “James Bond” franchise and “Mission Impossible,” the royal had a firm response.
“James Bond, 100%,” he said. “I want to make sure that that is in good hands.”
Harry joins others in the royal family, who have responded warmly to the news. On Nov. 16, the official X account of King Charles and Queen Camilla shared a post about the casting.
“Welcome to His Majesty’s Secret Service, Mr Bond,” the post read.
MI6, the UK’s foreign intelligence agency for which the fictional Bond works, also gave its approval.
“We’ve been expecting you… 👀” the agency wrote in a comment under the announcement.
Pierce Brosnan, who portrayed James Bond across seven years and four films, had fans particularly emotional after sharing a post in which he welcomed Pattinson into “the world of Bond.”
“Dear Robert, Welcome to the world of Bond,” Brosnan wrote in the post. “You are going to be magnificent.”
Another actor who portrayed the iconic agent, George Lazenby, also had some advice for the new 007.
“Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world,” Lazenby, who played Bond in 1969’s “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service.” “But remember to enjoy yourself.”

title: Merry Christmas, Ya Filthy Animals! Macaulay Culkin To Return To Star in ‘Home Alone’ Sequel
summary: A new “Home Alone” sequel by Disney is in the works, and it stars none other than Macaulay Culkin, the original actor behind the mischievous lead character, NBC News has confirmed.  Digital media outlet Puck first reported the news of the project Nov. 20.
story: Bad news for the wet bandits, it looks like the Kevin McCallister is back.

A new “Home Alone” sequel by Disney is in the works, and it stars none other than Macaulay Culkin, the original actor behind the mischievous lead character, NBC News has confirmed.  Digital media outlet Puck first reported the news of the project Nov. 20.
The sequel will be written and produced by Seth Rogen and longtime writing and producing partner Evan Goldberg, a source with knowledge of the project confirmed to NBC News.
A spokesperson for Disney declined to comment on the project.

The 1990 hit Christmas movie revolved around Kevin, a kid whose family mistakenly left him at home when leaving for vacation. Left to his own devices in an empty house, Kevin revels in his freedom. But when burglars Marv and Harry, played by Joe Pesci and Daniel Stern, attempt to break into the home, Kevin is forced to defend his turf.

The film was among the most successful comedy movies of its time, grossing $285.8 million domestically upon its release — a number made even more impressive when considering it was made on an estimated $18 million budget.

Culkin starred in a second film in the franchise, “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York,” which opened in 1992. The sequel wasn’t quite the smash hit that the original film was, but it was still considered a box office success.
Over the years, four more movies were made as part of the “Home Alone” franchise, however Culkin did not return to reprise his role.

Since, the actor has spoken out about his potential openness to returning to the role. In a conversation with the film’s director Chris Columbus last year, Culkin said that he envisioned a Kevin who’s a widower and raising a child on his own.

“He’s raising his kid and they don’t really get along, he’s working all the time,” Culkin said during the event, according to the Hollywood Reporter. “There’s one of two ways you can do it. One, he actually leaves the kid behind by mistake; he calls up his mom like, ‘So sorry, I get it now.’ Or I leave him behind on purpose, like, ‘Oh, that made me the man I am today.’”
Culkin most recently appeared as Kevin in an ad campaign, promoting McDonald’s “Home Alone” Meal, which will be available at participating restaurants nationwide starting Dec. 1.

title: ‘The Rainmaker’ Star Milo Callaghan Breaks Down Rudy and Sarah’s Relationship Turn in Episode 6
summary: “The Rainmaker” star Milo Callaghan talks Rudy and Sarah’s relationship in Season 2, Leo’s return and what fans can expect as the case heads to Ireland.
story: Warning: Spoilers from Season 2, Episode 6 of “The Rainmaker” below…
Rudy Baylor will stop at nothing to get justice for his clients, even if that means traveling over 3,000 miles for a possible showdown with an Irish crime boss.

Season 2 of USA Network’s “The Rainmaker” has raised the stakes, introducing multiple, life-threatening cases that Rudy, played by Milo Callaghan, Bruiser (Lana Parrilla) and Deck (P.J. Byrne) have to navigate. Anchoring the season is Rudy’s defense of client Victor Suffredes (Asher De Land), a young kid who is wrongfully being held in a juvenile detention center. Discrepancies in Victor’s case lead Rudy to unravel a for-profit prison scheme affecting hundreds of children.

“Part of the privilege of doing the show is that there’s a very real-world application to the information,” Callaghan tells TODAY.com about the Season 2 storyline. “The cases in the show are very real examples of injustice in the world, and I feel like the sanctity of childhood is generally held so high by the populace. But every now and then, people transgress that and they mistreat children for profit, and that’s the world that we’re living in in Season 2.”

The case takes a turn in Episode 6, which aired Friday, Nov. 20, when the gang decides to add Irish corporation Akram Holdings, the center’s parent company, as a defendant, meaning that the lawsuit will continue in Ireland. (Although the series is set in Charleston, South Carolina, the show is actually filmed in Dublin, Ireland).

There, fans will also learn more details about Sarah’s (Madison Iseman) involvement with the Irish Garda as she looks to clear her name and reputation. Speaking of Sarah, she and Rudy share an emotional moment during the episode when she confesses how she truly feels about her ex (and opposing counsel).

Below, Callaghan unpacks Episode 6’s biggest moments, including Rudy and Sarah’s heartfelt moment, and teases what fans can expect from the two of them the rest of the season. He also opens up about Richard Kind joining the cast as Deck’s dad and reveals if fans will see John Slattery’s Leo again.
This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

“It’s very easy in 10 hours of TV to create black and white binaries. I think Sarah truthfully gets a hard time at the end of Season 1. I think when you really delve into her thought process, like, I don’t think she’s a villain. She’s like Rudy. She was like a kid looking for fulfillment the way that she’d been raised to look for it, and she’s a product of her environment. As Rudy is at sea at the beginning of Season 2, so is Sarah. I don’t know if people ever change, but I think people always grow. For all the, kind of, anger at the way that she leveraged certain parts of his personal life in Season 1 for her own gain, I think he understands that people grow. Over the course of the season, I think maybe we’ll see if they can grow in a way that complements each other.”
“I think that everybody has the opportunity for redemption.”

“He’s a complete rapscallion, is the word that I would use. He’s like a rascal in the best sense of the word. He’s generous. He projects this kind of certainty. Film sets are places where a lot can go wrong. Often when you’re working with a cast and a crew…you want people to come onto that set with a sense of purpose. He embodies purpose. He’s hilarious. He is kind. He’s a stunning actor and just gave us all a lot of time and energy that we were all really grateful for. We had to bring Richard Kind to Ireland, and that was not the easiest sell, I don’t think, for him. Maybe it was. You’d have to ask him. But he showed up with his heart and soul, and just made the experience even more special than it already was.”

“We both are. I work with P.J. more than anyone else on the show. We have a shorthand that makes those days very easy and very productive. I mean, he’s the master of improvisation, but also just presence. Like, he often will say, “Just be with me,” and those are the scenes I feel where we’ve had not enough time to prep, and where it’s just me and him, that are some of my favorite to shoot. He’s fantastic.”
“I do. I don’t think you’ve seen it yet.”

“John’s the don. He really was such a grounding influence for me in Season 1, and was so generous with his time. I have a lot to thank him for. Having him back was just a privilege. He only came back for a short time. We managed to squeeze it in around other commitments, and we were really grateful he agreed to do it. I think he really is a classy part of the show, and he’s a fantastic actor.
I think, if you stick with it there, yeah, you get to see Rudy interact with him.”

“I think they each bring their own kind of Medusa-esque fears for him. Rudy doesn’t like bullies. The thing about Rudy is he’ll hit a bully. I think in different ways they all, in his eyes, embody the characteristics of a bully. The other thing that I think is that he really has a lot of compassion. He’s learnt a lot since Season 1, and I think he looks at people like Amanda Vaughn and he doesn’t agree with them. I think he understands them a lot more than maybe he used to. Amanda Vaughn’s a pretty stunning adversary, though.

(For Sarah), it’s very personal. I think (showrunner Michael Seitzman) said to us before we started shooting that ‘They’re like a bird and a fish who fell in love, but where are they going to live?’ And I really think that even at the end of Season 1, they’re still a bird and a fish who fell in love, figuring out if they have a place to live or not. One of them is going to have to make sacrifices. Do you ever really let go of somebody that you had that very early earnest love with? I don’t know. I think he feels that in his chest in a way that I think he can otherwise make sense of with Leo and Amanda. I think Sarah is somebody who will always touch his nerves in some way.”

“It’s so fun. We go to Ireland. It’s the start of the next episode. We shoot the show in Dublin … we shot exteriors in Charleston, but a lot of the show’s interiors take place in Dublin, and we all have such an affinity with the country, the city particularly. We arrive in Dublin as a three. As actors, we spent a year and a half in Dublin, shooting two seasons of the show. It really felt like coming home. Also they’re fish out of water. When you’re an American in America, everything, no matter how big it is, it’s normal. We had quite a lot of fun playing with this idea of Americans in a completely new environment, completely new culture that’s a little bit maybe more muted.

I work with P.J. and Lana, and they’re Americans, and we shoot in Ireland. Culturally, PJ is one of the loudest people you’ve ever met in my life, right? Even by American standards, he’s so big. He’s so charismatic and so generous with his energy. Then sometimes when we walk around Dublin together, people are like, ‘What is happening? Who is this bundle of energy?’ We play a lot with those cultural differences, which is really fun.”

“For me, it’s because it’s not a legal drama. It’s really about people. We hang it on the coat hanger of the courts. But really, it’s a thriller. It’s a detective buddy cop movie. There’s romance in it. There’s comedy. We have a really like neo-noir, dark edge to it. I’m really grateful that this first season is getting this life on Amazon because I really think we stepped it up in Season 2. It was always the goal for people to have the opportunity to watch Season 1, so that that would be an off ramp, and they could jump into Season 2. Season 2 felt like it came alive. We felt like we were a team that’d been playing together for years, instead of trying to find our feet and figuring out colors and tones. Also we just have such a wonderful crew and cast. It’s such a massive ensemble. I think everybody says that their show has the best cast and crew in the world. So somebody has to be lying somewhere. But I really stand by the fact that my cast and my crew are the best of the best.”

title: ‘Abbott Elementary’ Star Janelle James Says She ‘Bullied’ Her Way Into a Role in ‘GTA VI’: ‘Dream Come True’
summary: Janelle James of “Abbott Elementary” explains how she landed a role voicing a radio host in “Grand Theft Auto VI.”
story: If you recognize the voice of a certain radio host in the midst of committing motorized mayhem while playing “Grand Theft Auto VI,” you’re not imagining things.
Comedian and “Abbott Elementary” star Janelle James says she “bullied” her way into being included in the blockbuster video game because she is a diehard fan of the “GTA” series.

James is featured as a radio host in the game, which was released to acclaim on Nov. 19 after a 13-year wait since the last edition of “GTA.” She shared the lengths she went to in order to secure her role in a social media post.

“It’s very important to me that everybody knows that not only is that me, I’m not simply ‘voice acting,’” she wrote on her Instagram story Nov. 19. “I pursued, conceptualized, pitched, scripted AND voice acted my radio show.”
James added that she cast comedian friends Zainab Johnson and Liza Treyger on her show on the game, which was created by Rockstar Games.
“Rockstar didn’t ‘choose’ me, I bullied my way to them,” James wrote. “I’ve been playing this game since Vice City and this is a literal dream come true!!”
“Vice City” is an earlier version of the game that was released in 2002.

“GTA VI” allows players to toggle between the characters of Jason, a military veteran with a history of working with drug runners, and his girlfriend, Lucia, a fighter who was recently released from prison. The main characters are voiced by Dylan Rourke and Manni L. Perez.

Gamers had already been speculating that it was James’ voice they were hearing before she confirmed it. James, who plays principal Ava Coleman on “Abbott Elementary,” was instantly recognizable to people playing the game when it first came out.
“Janelle James from Abbott Elementary?!?!?!” one fan wrote on X with a clip from the game with James’ radio show playing.
“Janelle james in gta 6 radio just made this game 100 times better,” another wrote.
“NOT AVA BEING IN GTA 6 LMFAOOO ICONIC,” another posted.
James, 47, also responded to the outpouring of support in her post.
“I’m told the response is already great, TY,” she wrote. “Hope to catch ya’ll in these online streets where I will promptly kick you square in your back then put two in your dome. Cheers!!!”

title: Where Are Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison of ‘The Altruists’ Now?
summary: Two of the central figures involved in the collapse of the cryptocurrency exchange FTX into bankruptcy and subsequent trials for fraud have returned to the spotlight four years later.
story: Two of the central figures involved in the collapse of the cryptocurrency exchange FTX into bankruptcy and subsequent trials for fraud have returned to the spotlight four years later.

The new scripted Netflix series “The Altruists,” which begins streaming on Nov. 19, dramatizes the dynamic between Sam Bankman-Fried and his former girlfriend, Caroline Ellison, as they tried to remake the global financial system only for the company to implode in scandal.
Emmy-winning “Ozark” star Julia Garner portrays Ellison, and “Say Nothing” actor Anthony Boyle plays Bankman-Fried in the new series.
Boyle spoke on TODAY Nov. 20 about how he had “a lot of source material” about Bankman-Fried to prepare for the role because of all the interviews he did during FTX’s rise and fall.

“Because there was so much written about him, there was so many different aspects of him from different angles,” Boyle told Craig Melvin, Dylan Dreyer and Al Roker. “So some people thought he was a villain, some people thought he was the white knight of crypto, so I had a lot to draw on.”
Boyle said he also corresponded with Bankman-Fried via email from prison, where Bankman-Fried is serving a 25-year sentence.
“I was really bowled over by his intelligence,” Boyle said. “Even through emails I was like, ‘This guy is a savant.’ He’s so, so clever. Really, really interesting guy.”
Here is what to know about Bankman-Fried and Ellison, how their relationship dissolved, and where they are now.
Who Is Sam Bankman-Fried?
Bankman-Fried, 34, is the co-founder of the Bahamas-based FTX cryptocurrency exchange, which he started in 2019, as well as the crypto trading firm Alameda Research.
FTX became one of the world’s biggest cryptocurrency trading platforms and was valued at more than $30 billion at its peak before filing for bankruptcy in November 2022.

Bankman-Fried, an MIT graduate and son of Stanford professors, also was a prominent figure in the effective altruism movement, which is where the name of the Netflix series “The Altruists” comes from.

Effective altruism is a philosophical movement popular in Silicon Valley that includes the model of “earn to give,” meaning to make as much money as possible in order to give it away for the benefit of mankind, according to NBC News.

The movement is based on the premise that “people ought to do good in the most clear-sighted, ambitious, and unsentimental way possible,” according to a 2022 profile of effective altruism by The New Yorker.

Bankman-Fried ingrained those principles into Alameda Research and FTX, arguing that making large amounts of money would be beneficial because it would then be given away to help others. At one point, his net worth was estimated at $24 billion, according to NBC News.

A slogan that is used in the Netflix series is “all in, all the time,” meaning the altruistic decision is to always pursue the possibility of more money, even if it’s risky, because it can do the most good.

“I think Sam and Caroline both believed that the ends justified the means,” show-runner Graham Moore told Netflix’s Tudum. “Until the FBI showed up, and they found out there was a point at which that doesn’t work anymore.”

When FTX collapsed, Bankman-Fried’s mentor and a leader of the effective altruism movement, Will McAskill, disavowed him. He tweeted in 2022 that if Bankman-Fried “lied and misused customer funds he betrayed me, just as he betrayed his customers, his employees, his investors, & the communities he was a part of.”
Who Is Caroline Ellison?

Ellison, 32, is a Stanford graduate and Bankman-Fried’s former girlfriend and employee. She first met him when they were both working at the Wall Street firm Jane Street out of college in 2016, and she was introduced to the effective altruism movement by him.
She became a trader at Alameda Research in 2018 and then was elevated to co-CEO in 2021, according to a news release by the company.
Ellison and Bankman-Fried began dating in 2020 and broke up in 2022, Bankman-Fried testified at his trial in 2023, according to The Wall Street Journal.
“She wanted more from it than I was able to give,” he said.
What Happened to Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison?
Ellison went from being in a romantic relationship with Bankman-Fried to testifying against him during his trial in 2023.

A jury found Bankman-Fried guilty on all seven criminal counts against him in November 2023, which included being convicted of wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud against FTX customers and against Alameda Research lenders, conspiracy to commit securities fraud and conspiracy to commit commodities fraud against FTX investors, and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

Bankman-Fried, who pleaded not guilty to all the charges, was accused along with other FTX executives of making risky investments with billions of dollars stolen from customer accounts and using funds looted from the company to buy real estate in the Caribbean and make political donations.

Ellison’s lawyers said during her trial that Bankman-Fried had persuaded her to stay at Alameda by saying he loved her and the business needed her “while also perversely demonstrating that he considered her not good enough to be seen in public with him at high-profile events,” according to NBC News.

Ellison cooperated with federal investigators as they built their case against Bankman-Fried. Prosecutors said in a court filing ahead of her sentencing in September 2024 that Ellison’s testimony was “a cornerstone of the trial.”

Her lawyers wrote in the document that Bankman-Fried directed Ellison to help “steal billions” while she lived “in dread, knowing that a disastrous collapse was likely, but fearing that disentangling herself would only hasten that collapse,” according to NBC News.

In December 2022, Ellison accepted a plea deal on charges of financial fraud and conspiracy and cooperated with investigators in outlining the inner workings at FTX and Alameda Research, according to a court filing.
Where is Caroline Ellison Now?
Ellison was sentenced to two years in prison in September 2024 for conspiracy and fraud after taking the plea deal two years earlier.
She had faced a maximum sentence of about 110 years, but received two years due to her cooperation with federal investigators.
U.S. District Judge Lewis A. Kaplan also ordered her to forfeit $11 billion for her involvement in the collapse of FTX.
She began serving her sentence on Nov. 7, 2024, at a federal prison in Danbury, Connecticut, according to The Associated Press.
She did not end up serving the full two years. Ellison was released from federal custody on Jan. 21, 2026 after serving about 14 months, according to records from the Federal Bureau of Prisons.
She then quickly landed a job once she was released and returned to her effective altruism roots.

In a Substack post in September, the founder of Manifund, a philanthropic platform tied to the effective altruism movement, wrote that Ellison had joined the company in August. He wrote that she was hired “to develop our funding platform and research how to effectively direct philanthropic dollars.”
Where Is Sam Bankman-Fried Now?
After being convicted by a jury on all seven criminal counts against him in 2023, Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison in March 2024 for orchestrating the FTX fraud.
In addition to his prison sentence, he was ordered to pay $11 billion in forfeiture.

Bankman-Fried spoke with Tucker Carlson from Brooklyn’s Metropolitan Detention Center in New York City in March 2025, where he shared details about his then-cell block mate Sean “Diddy” Combs and his life in prison.
“It’s sort of dystopian,” Bankman-Fried said. “You know, the fortunate thing, the place I’m in, I’m not in ... I’m not in physical danger.”
In June 2026, a three-judge panel of the Manhattan-based 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied his appeal to have his conviction overturned.
He is currently incarcerated at FCI Lompoc I, a low-security federal institution in Lompoc, California, according to the Federal Bureau of Prisons. His release date is listed as Dec. 15, 2043.

title: Beyoncé Sings ‘Irreplaceable’ in Spanish on TODAY in 2007
summary: Beyoncé performed “Irreplaceable” on TODAY in 2007, switching it up and singing it in Spanish.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Beyoncé singing in Spanish on the plaza on April 2, 2007.
Beyoncé put on a show quite unlike anything fans were expecting when she performed on TODAY on April 2, 2007.

The iconic singer did a rendition of her hit “Irreplaceable,” that featured her adding lyrics from the Spanish-language version “Irreemplazable.” The song was featured in the deluxe edition of “B’Day,” which was released the day after her TODAY appearance.
“How y’all feeling this beautiful morning?” she asked at the top of the performance while perched on a stool, with a guitarist and bassist seated next to her and a band behind them.
Beyoncé Greets the Crowd and Switched Things Up
With a huge crowd surrounding her at the Plaza, the singer kicked off the track by encouraging them to sing along with her.
“I’m doing this acoustic style because I need y’all’s help. Are y’all going to sing this song with me? Y’all know what to do, right? Yeah? Here we go. Sing with me.”
She then launched into “Irreplaceable.”
“Y’all can be a little louder, right?” she said, shortly after starting the song.
She went nearly 90 seconds before she changed things up.
“So, you know what? I want to do something a little different. So I need y’all to be quiet and listen. This right here is for my Latino fans,” she said before singing in Spanish.
Translating the ‘Irreemplazable’ Lyrics
The translation for what she sang veers a little from the English lyrics of the song. Her Spanish lyrics translated to the following:
You see my love, this time I forgot you
In the closet, tucked away in a corner are your things
This is over
I swear I can’t stand you anymore
I don’t want you anymore, neither as a lover
This time you won’t win
You can leave and never come back
And if you think this time I will forgive you
You’ll see that you’ll never deceive me again
Just get out of here
An Energetic Ending and Cheers From the Crowd
She proceeded to sing about 40 seconds in Spanish before going back to English for the chorus and the remainder of the song.
After she finished, the crowd thunderously cheered.
